title: KYC Policy Adoption
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: All NBFCs are, therefore, advised to adopt the same with suitable modifications depending on the activity undertaken by them and ensure that a proper policy framework on ‘Know Your Customer’ and Anti-Money Laundering measures is formulated and put in place with the approval of the Board within three months of the date of this circular.
description: NBFCs must adopt a KYC policy framework with the approval of the Board within three months of the circular date.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must create and approve a KYC policy within three months. This policy must be tailored to their specific activities. The policy ensures that NBFCs know their customers and prevent money laundering.
violation_message_template: NBFC {account_id} failed to adopt a KYC policy within three months of the circular date {flag_date}.

title: Customer Information Confidentiality
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: While preparing operational guidelines NBFCs may bear in mind that the information collected from the customer for the purpose of opening of account should be kept as confidential and not divulge any details thereof for cross selling or any other purposes.
description: NBFCs must keep customer information confidential and not use it for cross-selling or other purposes.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must keep customer information secret and not use it for other purposes. They should only collect information relevant to the customer's risk profile.
violation_message_template: NBFC {account_id} failed to keep customer {customer_id} information confidential on {flag_date}.

title: KYC Guidelines for Brokers/Agents
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Adherence to Know Your Customer (KYC) guidelines by NBFC and persons authorised by NBFCs including brokers/agents etc.
description: NBFCs and their brokers/agents must adhere to KYC guidelines.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs and their brokers/agents must follow KYC guidelines. They must know their customers and prevent money laundering.
violation_message_template: NBFC {account_id} and its brokers/agents failed to adhere to KYC guidelines on {flag_date}.

title: KYC Compliance Responsibility
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: it shall be the sole responsibility of the NBFC to ensure full compliance with the KYC guidelines by such persons.
description: NBFCs are responsible for ensuring KYC compliance by persons authorized by them, including brokers/agents.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must ensure that brokers/agents comply with KYC guidelines. If they don't, the NBFC is responsible. This is to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing.
violation_message_template: NBFC {account_id} failed to ensure KYC compliance by broker/agent {customer_id} for transaction {transaction_id} on {transaction_date}

title: KYC Guidelines for New Customers
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: In respect of new customers acquired after April 1, 2004, KYC guidelines as stated in the circular CC No.48 should be complied with in all cases.
description: RNBCs must comply with KYC guidelines for new customers acquired after April 1, 2004.
plain_english: This means: RNBCs must follow KYC guidelines for all new customers. This helps prevent money laundering and terrorist financing.
violation_message_template: RNBC {account_id} failed to comply with KYC guidelines for new customer {customer_id} acquired on {transaction_date}

title: KYC Guidelines for Existing Customers
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: For the existing customers, initially, KYC guidelines should be complied in respect of large customers whose aggregate deposit exceeds Rs.1 lakh.
description: RNBCs must comply with KYC guidelines for existing customers with aggregate deposits over Rs.1 lakh.
plain_english: This means: RNBCs must follow KYC guidelines for existing customers with large deposits. This helps prevent money laundering and terrorist financing.
violation_message_template: RNBC {account_id} failed to comply with KYC guidelines for existing customer {customer_id} with aggregate deposit {amount} exceeding Rs.1 lakh

title: Due Diligence for Authorized Persons
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs should put in place a process of due diligence in respect of persons authorised by NBFCs including brokers/agents etc.
description: NBFCs must conduct due diligence on persons authorized by them, including brokers/agents.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must investigate brokers/agents to ensure they are trustworthy. This helps prevent money laundering and terrorist financing.
violation_message_template: NBFC {account_id} failed to conduct due diligence on broker/agent {customer_id} authorized on {transaction_date}

title: Deposit Receipt Requirements
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: All deposit receipts should bear the name and Registered Office address of the NBFC and must invariably indicate the name of the persons authorised by NBFCs including brokers/agents etc. and their addresses who mobilised the deposit and the link office with the telephone number of such officer and/or persons authorised by NBFCs including brokers/agents etc
description: NBFCs must ensure that deposit receipts contain required information, including the name and address of the NBFC, the name and address of the person who mobilised the deposit, and the link office with telephone number.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must include specific details on deposit receipts to ensure transparency and identifiable contact with depositors. This includes the NBFC's name and address, the name and address of the person who collected the deposit, and the link office with telephone number.
violation_message_template: Deposit receipt {transaction_id} dated {transaction_date} is missing required information, including the name and address of the NBFC and the person who mobilised the deposit.

title: Audit and Inspection Requirements
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: the companies should have systems in place to ensure that the books of accounts of persons authorised by NBFCs including brokers/agents etc, so far as they relate to brokerage functions of the company, are available for audit and inspection whenever required
description: NBFCs must have systems in place to ensure that the books of accounts of persons authorised by them, including brokers/agents, are available for audit and inspection.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must ensure that the financial records of their agents and brokers are available for audit and inspection at all times to maintain transparency and accountability.
violation_message_template: The books of accounts of person {customer_id} authorised by NBFC are not available for audit and inspection.

title: Simplified KYC Procedure
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Hence, it has been decided to further simplify the KYC procedure for opening accounts by NBFCs for those persons who intend to keep balances not exceeding rupees fifty thousand (Rs. 50,000/-) in all their accounts taken together and the total credit in all the accounts taken together is not expected to exceed rupees one lakh (Rs. 1,00,000/-) in a year.
description: NBFCs may open accounts with simplified KYC procedure for low-income individuals with balances not exceeding Rs. 50,000 and total credit not exceeding Rs. 1,00,000 in a year.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs can open accounts for low-income individuals with simplified KYC if they meet certain balance and credit limits. If the customer's balance or credit exceeds these limits, they must provide full KYC documents.
violation_message_template: Account {account_id} of customer {customer_name} has exceeded the balance limit of Rs. 50,000 or credit limit of Rs. 1,00,000. Full KYC documents are required to continue transactions.

title: Introduction Requirement
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: introduction from another account holder who has been subjected to full KYC procedure. The introducer’s account with the NBFC should be at least six month old and should show satisfactory transactions.
description: NBFCs may open accounts with introduction from an existing account holder who has undergone full KYC procedure.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs can open accounts for new customers with introduction from an existing customer who has completed full KYC procedure.
violation_message_template: Account {account_id} of customer {customer_name} does not have a valid introduction from an existing account holder.

title: Balance Limit Notification
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: the customer should be made aware that if at any point of time, the balances in all his/her accounts with the NBFC (taken together) exceeds rupees fifty thousand (Rs. 50,000/-) or total credit in the account exceeds rupees one lakh (Rs. 1,00,000/-), no further transactions will be permitted until the full KYC procedure is completed.
description: NBFCs must notify customers when their balance reaches Rs. 40,000 or total credit reaches Rs. 80,000 to submit full KYC documents.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must notify customers when their balance or credit reaches certain limits to prevent account suspension.
violation_message_template: Account {account_id} of customer {customer_name} has reached the balance limit of Rs. 40,000 or credit limit of Rs. 80,000. Full KYC documents are required to continue transactions.

title: Customer Identification
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: It was further clarified to NBFCs in April 2008 that for the purpose of Circular dated February 21, 2005 the term 'being satisfied' means that the NBFC must be able to satisfy the competent authorities that due diligence was observed based on the risk profile of the customer in compliance with the extant guidelines in place.
description: NBFCs must observe due diligence based on the risk profile of the customer and satisfy competent authorities that guidelines are being followed.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must verify customer identities by following guidelines and being able to prove it to authorities. They should not deny services based on a fixed list of documents, but rather consider the risk profile of each customer.
violation_message_template: NBFC {account_id} failed to verify customer {customer_name} identity for account {account_id} as per guidelines.

title: Address Verification
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: It is clarified that permanent correct address, as referred to in Annex-VIII of this circular, means the address at which a person usually resides and can be taken as the address as mentioned in a utility bill or any other document accepted by the NBFC for verification of the address of the customer.
description: NBFCs must verify the permanent address of customers using a utility bill or other accepted documents.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must check the customer's permanent address using a utility bill or other documents, and can use supplementary evidence like a letter for further verification.
violation_message_template: NBFC {account_id} failed to verify address of customer {customer_name} for account {account_id}.

title: Periodic Review Risk Categorisation
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs are required to put in place a system of periodical review of risk categorisation of accounts and the need for applying enhanced due diligence measures in case of higher risk perception on a customer.
description: NBFCs must review risk categorisation of accounts periodically and apply enhanced due diligence measures for higher risk customers.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must regularly review customer accounts to determine the risk level and apply extra checks for high-risk customers to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing.
violation_message_template: NBFC failed to review risk categorisation of account {account_id} for customer {customer_id} within the required six-month period.

title: Customer Identification Data Updation
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs also introduce a system of periodical updation of customer identification data (including photograph/s) after the account is opened.
description: NBFCs must update customer identification data periodically after account opening.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must regularly update customer identification data, including photos, to ensure accuracy and prevent identity fraud.
violation_message_template: NBFC failed to update customer identification data for account {account_id} within the required five-year period for low-risk customers or two-year period for high and medium-risk customers.

title: KYC/AML Guidelines for Overseas Branches
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: KYC/AML guidelines issued by Reserve Bank of India shall also apply to their branches and majority owned subsidiaries located outside India, especially, in countries which do not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations, to the extent local laws permit.
description: NBFCs must apply KYC/AML guidelines to overseas branches and subsidiaries.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must follow Indian KYC/AML guidelines for their overseas branches and subsidiaries, especially in countries with weak anti-money laundering regulations.
violation_message_template: NBFC failed to apply KYC/AML guidelines to overseas branch {branch_id} located in {country}.

title: Suspicious Transaction Reporting
act_section: PMLA Rules
source_clause: Suspicious transaction should include inter alia transactions which give rise to a reasonable ground of suspicion that these may involve financing of the activities relating to terrorism.
description: NBFCs must report suspicious transactions to the Financial Intelligence Unit – India (FIU-IND).
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must identify and report suspicious transactions that may be related to terrorist financing to the FIU-IND.
violation_message_template: NBFC failed to report suspicious transaction {transaction_id} to the FIU-IND.

title: UNSCR List Update
act_section: Sections 45K and 45L of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
source_clause: NBFCs should ensure to update the consolidated list of individuals and entities as circulated by Reserve Bank.
description: NBFCs must update the list of individuals and entities as per the UNSCR list circulated by the Reserve Bank.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must regularly update their list of sanctioned individuals and entities to prevent transactions with them. This is a critical requirement to prevent misuse of banking channels.
violation_message_template: NBFC failed to update the UNSCR list, potentially allowing transactions with sanctioned individuals/entities {customer_name} on {transaction_date}

title: New Account Screening
act_section: Sections 45K and 45L of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
source_clause: NBFCs are advised that before opening any new account it should be ensured that the name/s of the proposed customer does not appear in the list.
description: NBFCs must screen new customers against the UNSCR list before opening an account.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must check if a new customer is on the UNSCR list before opening an account to prevent transactions with sanctioned individuals/entities.
violation_message_template: NBFC failed to screen new customer {customer_name} against the UNSCR list on {transaction_date}

title: Existing Account Screening
act_section: Sections 45K and 45L of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
source_clause: NBFCs should scan all existing accounts to ensure that no account is held by or linked to any of the entities or individuals included in the list.
description: NBFCs must regularly scan existing accounts against the UNSCR list.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must periodically check their existing accounts to ensure that no account is held by or linked to sanctioned individuals/entities.
violation_message_template: NBFC failed to scan existing account {account_id} against the UNSCR list on {transaction_date}

title: Suspicious Transaction Reporting
act_section: Sections 45K and 45L of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
source_clause: Full details of accounts bearing resemblance with any of the individuals/entities in the list should immediately be intimated to RBI and FIU-IND.
description: NBFCs must report suspicious transactions to RBI and FIU-IND.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must immediately report any suspicious transactions related to sanctioned individuals/entities to the RBI and FIU-IND.
violation_message_template: NBFC failed to report suspicious transaction {transaction_id} to RBI and FIU-IND on {transaction_date}

title: Recruitment Screening
act_section: Sections 45K and 45L of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
source_clause: It would, therefore, be necessary that adequate screening mechanism is put in place by NBFCs as an integral part of their recruitment/hiring process of personnel.
description: NBFCs must implement adequate screening mechanisms for new recruits.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must have a proper screening process in place for new employees to prevent the hiring of individuals who may misuse the banking/financial channels.
violation_message_template: NBFC failed to implement adequate screening for new recruit {employee_name} on {hire_date}

title: PEP Account Monitoring
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: In the event of an existing customer or the beneficial owner of an existing account, subsequently becoming a PEP, NBFCs (including RNBCs) should obtain senior management approval to continue the business relationship and subject the account to the CDD measures as applicable to the customers of PEP category including enhanced monitoring on an ongoing basis.
description: NBFCs must obtain senior management approval and apply CDD measures to PEP accounts.
plain_english: This means: If a customer becomes a Politically Exposed Person, the NBFC must get senior management approval to continue the business relationship and monitor the account closely. The NBFC must apply Customer Due Diligence measures to the account.
violation_message_template: PEP account {account_id} of {customer_name} requires senior management approval and enhanced monitoring.

title: Principal Officer Independence
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs (including RNBCs) should ensure that the Principal Officer is able to act independently and report directly to the senior management or to the Board of Directors.
description: The Principal Officer must be able to act independently and report directly to senior management or the Board of Directors.
plain_english: This means: The Principal Officer must be able to make decisions without interference and report directly to senior management or the Board of Directors.
violation_message_template: Principal Officer {customer_name} is not able to act independently.

title: High Risk Country Monitoring
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: All NBFCs and RNBCs are accordingly advised to take into account risks arising from the deficiencies in AML/CFT regime of Uzbekistan, Iran, Pakistan, Turkmenistan, Sao Tome and Principe on the subject.
description: NBFCs must monitor transactions from high-risk countries.
plain_english: This means: If a transaction involves a high-risk country, the NBFC must monitor it closely. The high-risk countries are Uzbekistan, Iran, Pakistan, Turkmenistan, and Sao Tome and Principe.
violation_message_template: Transaction {transaction_id} from high-risk country {country} requires monitoring.

title: Customer Due Diligence
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs were advised to carry out full scale customer due diligence (CDD) before opening an account whenever there is suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing or when other factors give rise to a belief that the customer does not, in fact, pose a low risk
description: NBFCs must perform full-scale customer due diligence before opening an account if there is suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing
plain_english: This means: If a customer seems suspicious, NBFCs must do a full background check before opening an account. This helps prevent money laundering and terrorist financing.
violation_message_template: Customer {customer_id} with account {account_id} did not undergo full CDD before account opening on {transaction_date}, potentially allowing money laundering or terrorist financing

title: STR Filing
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: In the circumstances when a NBFC believes that it would no longer be satisfied that it knows the true identity of the account holder, the Company should also file an STR with FIU-IND
description: NBFCs must file an STR with FIU-IND if they are no longer satisfied with the true identity of the account holder
plain_english: This means: If an NBFC is unsure about a customer's identity, they must file a suspicious transaction report with FIU-IND to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing
violation_message_template: Account {account_id} of customer {customer_id} did not have a filed STR with FIU-IND on {transaction_date} despite uncertainty about true identity

title: PEP Approval and CDD
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: In the event of an existing customer or the beneficial owner of an existing account, subsequently becoming a PEP, NBFCs (including RNBCS) were advised to obtain senior management approval to continue the business relationship and subject the account to the CDD measures as applicable to the customers of PEP
description: NBFCs must obtain senior management approval and perform CDD on existing customers who become PEPs
plain_english: This means: If an existing customer becomes a politically exposed person, NBFCs must get senior management approval to continue the business relationship and perform enhanced due diligence
violation_message_template: Customer {customer_id} became a PEP on {transaction_date} but did not receive senior management approval and enhanced CDD for account {account_id}

title: PEP Account Monitoring
act_section: Section 45K and 45L of Reserve Bank of India Regulation Act, 1934
source_clause: NBFCs should have appropriate ongoing risk management procedures for identifying and applying enhanced CDD to PEPs, customers who are close relatives of PEPs, and accounts of which PEP is the ultimate beneficial owner.
description: NBFCs must have ongoing risk management procedures for PEP accounts, including enhanced CDD for PEPs and their close relatives.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must monitor PEP accounts closely and apply enhanced CDD to PEPs, their close relatives, and accounts where PEP is the ultimate beneficial owner. This is to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing.
violation_message_template: PEP account {account_id} of {customer_name} has not undergone enhanced CDD, as required by regulatory guidelines.

title: Principal Officer Responsibilities
act_section: Section 45K and 45L of Reserve Bank of India Regulation Act, 1934
source_clause: The role and responsibilities of the Principal Officer should include overseeing and ensuring overall compliance with regulatory guidelines on KYC/AML/CFT issued from time to time and obligations under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, rules and regulations made thereunder, as amended form time to time.
description: The Principal Officer is responsible for ensuring overall compliance with KYC/AML/CFT guidelines and PMLA obligations.
plain_english: This means: The Principal Officer must oversee and ensure that the NBFC complies with all KYC/AML/CFT guidelines and PMLA obligations, including regulatory updates and amendments.
violation_message_template: Principal Officer has not ensured compliance with KYC/AML/CFT guidelines and PMLA obligations for {account_id} of {customer_name}.

title: Client Account Identification
act_section: Section 45K and 45L of Reserve Bank of India Regulation Act, 1934
source_clause: When the NBFC has knowledge or reason to believe that the client account opened by a professional intermediary is on behalf of a single client, that client must be identified.
description: NBFCs must identify the client when a professional intermediary opens an account on their behalf.
plain_english: This means: If an NBFC knows or suspects that a professional intermediary has opened an account for a single client, the NBFC must identify that client and apply KYC norms.
violation_message_template: Client account {account_id} opened by professional intermediary has not been identified, as required by KYC norms.

title: Beneficial Owner Identification
act_section: Section 45K and 45L of Reserve Bank of India Regulation Act, 1934
source_clause: beneficial owners must be identified. Where such funds are co-mingled at the NBFC, the NBFC should still look through to the beneficial owners.
description: NBFCs must identify and verify the beneficial owners of accounts, even if funds are co-mingled.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must identify the true owners of accounts and verify their identities, even if the funds are mixed with others. This is to prevent money laundering and ensure compliance with AML/CFT regulations.
violation_message_template: NBFC {account_id} has failed to identify and verify the beneficial owner(s) of the account, in violation of Section 45K and 45L of the RBI Regulation Act, 1934.

title: Professional Intermediaries Account Holding
act_section: Section 45K and 45L of Reserve Bank of India Regulation Act, 1934
source_clause: NBFCs should not allow opening and/or holding of an account on behalf of a client/s by professional intermediaries, like Lawyers and Chartered Accountants, etc.
description: NBFCs are prohibited from allowing professional intermediaries to hold accounts on behalf of clients if they cannot disclose the client's true identity.
plain_english: This means: Professional intermediaries like lawyers and accountants cannot hold accounts on behalf of their clients if they are bound by confidentiality and cannot disclose the client's true identity.
violation_message_template: NBFC {account_id} has allowed a professional intermediary to hold an account on behalf of a client, in violation of Section 45K and 45L of the RBI Regulation Act, 1934.

title: FATF Non-Compliant Countries
act_section: Section 45K and 45L of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
source_clause: NBFCs should give special attention to business relationships and transactions with persons (including legal persons and other financial institutions) from or in these countries.
description: NBFCs must monitor transactions with persons from countries that do not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs should carefully monitor transactions with persons from countries that do not follow FATF guidelines, as these transactions may pose a higher risk of money laundering or terrorism financing.
violation_message_template: Transaction {transaction_id} on {transaction_date} with {customer_name} from {country} requires special attention due to potential AML/CFT risks.

title: FATF High Risk Countries
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: All NBFCs/RNBCs were accordingly advised to take into account risks arising from the deficiencies in AML/CFT regime of these countries.
description: NBFCs/RNBCs must consider risks from countries with strategic AML/CFT deficiencies.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs/RNBCs must assess the risks of doing business with countries that have weak anti-money laundering and terrorist financing controls. This is to prevent the use of their services for illicit activities. Failure to do so may lead to regulatory action.
violation_message_template: Transaction {transaction_id} from {customer_name} with address in high-risk country {country} detected on {transaction_date}.
condition_value: Iran, Democratic People's Republic of Korea, Sao Tome and Principe

title: Money Laundering Prevention
act_section: Section 12 of PMLA, 2002
source_clause: NBFCs were advised to appoint a Principal Officer and put in place a system of internal reporting of suspicious transactions and cash transactions of Rs.10 lakh and above.
description: NBFCs must appoint a Principal Officer and establish a system for internal reporting of suspicious transactions and cash transactions exceeding Rs.10 lakh.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must have a Principal Officer and a system to report suspicious transactions and large cash transactions to prevent money laundering. This helps protect the financial system from illegal activities.
violation_message_template: NBFC {account_id} has failed to report a cash transaction of {amount} on {transaction_date}, exceeding the threshold of {threshold_value}.

title: Customer Account Information Preservation
act_section: Section 12 of PMLA, 2002
source_clause: Section 12 of the PMLA, 2002 casts certain obligations on the NBFCs in regard to preservation and reporting of customer account information.
description: NBFCs must preserve customer account information as per the provisions of PMLA, 2002.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must keep customer account information safe and secure, as required by the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002.
violation_message_template: NBFC {account_id} has failed to preserve customer account information for {record_age_years} years.

title: Cash Transaction Record
act_section: Section 12 of PMLA 2002
source_clause: NBFCs should introduce a system of maintaining proper record of transactions prescribed under Rule 3, as mentioned below: all cash transactions of the value of more than rupees ten lakh or its equivalent in foreign currency;
description: NBFCs must maintain records of cash transactions exceeding Rs. 10 lakh or its equivalent in foreign currency.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must keep records of large cash transactions. This includes transactions over Rs. 10 lakh or its equivalent in foreign currency. This is to prevent money laundering.
violation_message_template: Cash transaction of {amount} exceeded the threshold of Rs. 10 lakh on {transaction_date} for {customer_name}

title: Series of Cash Transactions Record
act_section: Section 12 of PMLA 2002
source_clause: all series of cash transactions integrally connected to each other which have been valued below rupees ten lakh or its equivalent in foreign currency where such series of transactions have taken place within a month and the aggregate value of such transactions exceeds rupees ten lakh;
description: NBFCs must maintain records of series of cash transactions that exceed Rs. 10 lakh in a month.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must keep records of multiple small cash transactions that add up to over Rs. 10 lakh in a month. This is to prevent money laundering.
violation_message_template: Series of cash transactions exceeded the threshold of Rs. 10 lakh on {transaction_date} for {customer_name}

title: Suspicious Transaction Record
act_section: Section 12 of PMLA 2002
source_clause: all suspicious transactions whether or not made in cash and in manner as mentioned in the Rules framed by Government of India under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002.
description: NBFCs must maintain records of suspicious transactions.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must keep records of suspicious transactions, whether made in cash or not. This is to prevent money laundering.
violation_message_template: Suspicious transaction detected on {transaction_date} for {customer_name}

title: Transaction Information Preservation
act_section: Section 12 of PMLA 2002
source_clause: NBFCs are required to maintain the following information in respect of transactions referred to in Rule 3:
description: NBFCs must preserve information about transactions, including nature, amount, date, and parties involved.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must keep information about transactions, including what happened, how much was involved, when it happened, and who was involved. This is to help with investigations.
violation_message_template: Transaction information not preserved for {transaction_id} on {transaction_date}

title: Record Maintenance and Preservation
act_section: Section 12 of PMLA 2002
source_clause: NBFCs should take appropriate steps to evolve a system for proper maintenance and preservation of account information in a manner that allows data to be retrieved easily and quickly whenever required or when requested by the competent authorities.
description: NBFCs must maintain and preserve account information for at least 10 years after the transaction is closed.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must keep account information safe and accessible for at least 10 years after the transaction is finished. This is to help with investigations.
violation_message_template: Account information not maintained for {account_id} after {days_overdue} days

title: Transaction Record Keeping
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs should ensure that records pertaining to the identification of the customer and his address are properly preserved for at least ten years after the business relationship is ended.
description: NBFCs must maintain records of customer identification and address for at least 10 years after the business relationship ends.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must keep records of customer identification and address for a long time. They must preserve these records for at least 10 years after the customer is no longer a customer. This is so that authorities can access these records if needed.
violation_message_template: NBFC failed to maintain records of customer {customer_id} identification and address for at least 10 years after the business relationship ended on {flag_date}.

title: Cash Transaction Reporting
act_section: PMLA rules
source_clause: NBFCs are required to report information relating to cash and suspicious transactions to the Director, Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND).
description: NBFCs must report cash and suspicious transactions to FIU-IND.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must send reports of cash and suspicious transactions to the authorities. They must follow the reporting formats and guidelines provided.
violation_message_template: NBFC failed to report cash transaction {transaction_id} of {amount} to FIU-IND on {transaction_date}.

title: Electronic Filing of CTR
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs are advised to initiate urgent steps to ensure electronic filing of cash transaction report (CTR) as early as possible.
description: NBFCs must initiate electronic filing of CTR as soon as possible.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must start sending cash transaction reports electronically as soon as possible. They must take urgent steps to make this happen.
violation_message_template: NBFC failed to initiate electronic filing of CTR by {flag_date}.

title: Cash Transaction Report Deadline
act_section: Sections 45K and 45L of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
source_clause: The cash transaction report (CTR) for each month should be submitted to FIU-IND by 15th of the succeeding month.
description: NBFCs must submit the cash transaction report for each month to FIU-IND by the 15th of the succeeding month.
plain_english: This means: The NBFC must file a cash transaction report with FIU-IND by the 15th of the next month. This report should include all cash transactions above Rs. 50,000. Failure to do so may result in regulatory action.
violation_message_template: Cash transaction report for {transaction_date} was not submitted to FIU-IND by the 15th of the succeeding month.

title: Suspicious Transaction Report Deadline
act_section: Sections 45K and 45L of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
source_clause: The Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) should be furnished within 7 days of arriving at a conclusion that any transaction, whether cash or non-cash, or a series of transactions integrally connected are of suspicious nature.
description: NBFCs must submit the suspicious transaction report to FIU-IND within 7 days of identifying a suspicious transaction.
plain_english: This means: The NBFC must file a suspicious transaction report with FIU-IND within 7 days of identifying a suspicious transaction. This report should include all relevant details of the suspicious transaction. Failure to do so may result in regulatory action.
violation_message_template: Suspicious transaction report for {transaction_date} was not submitted to FIU-IND within 7 days.

title: Principal Officer Responsibility
act_section: Sections 45K and 45L of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
source_clause: The Principal Officer will be responsible for timely submission of CTR and STR to FIU-IND;
description: The Principal Officer of the NBFC is responsible for ensuring timely submission of CTR and STR to FIU-IND.
plain_english: This means: The Principal Officer of the NBFC is responsible for ensuring that all cash transaction reports and suspicious transaction reports are submitted to FIU-IND on time. Failure to do so may result in regulatory action.
violation_message_template: Principal Officer failed to ensure timely submission of {report_type} to FIU-IND.

title: Confidentiality of Reports
act_section: Sections 45K and 45L of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
source_clause: Utmost confidentiality should be maintained in filing of CTR and STR with FIU-IND.
description: NBFCs must maintain utmost confidentiality when filing CTR and STR with FIU-IND.
plain_english: This means: The NBFC must keep all cash transaction reports and suspicious transaction reports confidential when filing them with FIU-IND. This means not disclosing the reports to anyone except the authorized personnel.
violation_message_template: Confidentiality of {report_type} was not maintained when filing with FIU-IND.

title: No Restrictions on Accounts with STR
act_section: Sections 45K and 45L of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
source_clause: NBFCs may not put any restrictions on operations in the accounts where an STR has been made.
description: NBFCs must not restrict operations on accounts where a suspicious transaction report has been filed.
plain_english: This means: The NBFC must not restrict any transactions on an account where a suspicious transaction report has been filed. However, the NBFC must ensure that there is no tipping off to the customer at any level.
violation_message_template: Restrictions were placed on account {account_id} after an STR was filed.

title: Customer Risk Profile
act_section: Prevention of Money-laundering (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005
source_clause: NBFCs are required to prepare a profile for each customer based on risk categorization.
description: NBFCs must prepare a customer profile based on risk categorization and review it periodically.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must create a customer profile based on risk, review it regularly, and update it as necessary to ensure effective transaction monitoring and suspicious transaction reporting.
violation_message_template: NBFC {customer_id} has not prepared a customer profile based on risk categorization for {customer_name}.

title: Transaction Monitoring Mechanism
act_section: Prevention of Money-laundering (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005
source_clause: NBFCs are required to put in place an appropriate software application to throw alerts when the transactions are inconsistent with risk categorization and updated profile of customers.
description: NBFCs must implement a transaction monitoring mechanism with alerts for inconsistent transactions.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must have a software system that alerts them to transactions that do not match the customer's risk profile, to help identify and report suspicious transactions.
violation_message_template: NBFC {customer_id} has not implemented a transaction monitoring mechanism with alerts for inconsistent transactions for {customer_name}.

title: Electronic Filing of CTR and STR
act_section: Prevention of Money-laundering (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005
source_clause: NBFCs were advised to initiate urgent steps to ensure electronic filing of cash transaction report (CTR) and Suspicious Transaction Reports (STR) to FIU-IND.
description: NBFCs must file CTR and STR electronically with FIU-IND.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must file cash transaction reports and suspicious transaction reports electronically with the Financial Intelligence Unit of India, as required.
violation_message_template: NBFC {customer_id} has not filed CTR and STR electronically with FIU-IND for {customer_name}.

title: Cash Transaction Reporting Threshold
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: In regard to CTR, it is reiterated that the cut-off limit of Rupees ten lakh is applicable to integrally connected cash transactions also.
description: NBFCs must report cash transactions exceeding Rs. 10 lakh to FIU-IND on a monthly basis.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must submit a report of cash transactions exceeding Rs. 10 lakh to FIU-IND every month. This report should include all individual cash transactions in an account during a calendar month where either debit or credit summation exceeds Rs. 10 lakh. However, transactions below Rs. 50,000 may not be indicated.
violation_message_template: Cash transaction of {amount} on {transaction_date} exceeds the threshold of {threshold_value} and must be reported to FIU-IND.

title: Cash Transaction Reporting Frequency
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs were advised to make Cash Transaction Reports (CTR) to FIU-India for every month latest by 15th of the succeeding month.
description: NBFCs must submit cash transaction reports to FIU-IND on a monthly basis.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must submit a report of cash transactions to FIU-IND every month, by the 15th of the next month.
violation_message_template: Cash transaction report for {transaction_date} is overdue and must be submitted to FIU-IND.

title: Integrally Connected Cash Transactions
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: For determining integrally connected cash transactions, NBFCs should take into account all individual cash transactions in an account during a calendar month, where either debit or credit summation, computed separately, exceeds Rupees ten lakh during the month.
description: NBFCs must consider all individual cash transactions in an account during a calendar month when determining integrally connected cash transactions.
plain_english: This means: When determining integrally connected cash transactions, NBFCs must consider all individual cash transactions in an account during a calendar month, where either debit or credit summation exceeds Rs. 10 lakh.
violation_message_template: Integrally connected cash transactions of {amount} on {transaction_date} exceed the threshold of {threshold_value} and must be reported to FIU-IND.

title: Counterfeit Currency Report
act_section: PMLA, 2002
source_clause: NBFCs are required to pay special attention to all complex, unusual large transactions and all unusual patterns of transactions, which have no apparent economic or visible lawful purpose.
description: NBFCs must report suspicious transactions to FIU-IND in the specified format.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must report suspicious transactions to FIU-IND immediately. This includes transactions where forgery of valuable security or documents has taken place. The report should be made in the specified format.
violation_message_template: Suspicious transaction {transaction_id} on {transaction_date} for {amount} has been reported to FIU-IND.

title: Suspicious Transaction Reporting
act_section: PMLA, 2002
source_clause: NBFCs should report all such attempted transactions in STRs, even if not completed by customers, irrespective of the amount of the transaction.
description: NBFCs must report attempted suspicious transactions to FIU-IND.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must report all attempted suspicious transactions to FIU-IND, even if the transaction was not completed.
violation_message_template: Attempted suspicious transaction {transaction_id} on {transaction_date} for {amount} has been reported to FIU-IND.

title: Record Keeping
act_section: PMLA, 2002
source_clause: These records are required to be preserved for ten years as is required under PMLA, 2002.
description: NBFCs must preserve records of suspicious transactions for 10 years.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must keep records of suspicious transactions for 10 years as required by PMLA, 2002.
violation_message_template: Records of suspicious transaction {transaction_id} on {transaction_date} have not been preserved for 10 years.

title: STR Filing
act_section: Rule 2(g) of Rules ibid
source_clause: NBFCs should make STRs if they have reasonable ground to believe that the transaction involve proceeds of crime generally irrespective of the amount of transaction
description: NBFCs must file STRs for transactions involving proceeds of crime.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must file STRs for transactions that involve proceeds of crime, regardless of the amount.
violation_message_template: Transaction {transaction_id} on {transaction_date} for {amount} involves proceeds of crime and has been reported to FIU-IND.

title: Record Preservation Period
act_section: Section 12 of PMLA, 2009
source_clause: The records referred to in clause (a) of Sub-Section (1) of Section 12 shall be maintained for a period of ten years from the date of transaction between the clients and the banking company and in terms of Sub-Section 2(b) of Section 12 of the Act ibid, the records referred to in clause (c) of Sub-Section (1) of Section 12 shall be maintained for a period of ten years from the date of cessation of transaction between the clients and the banking company.
description: NBFCs are required to maintain records of transactions for at least ten years from the date of transaction between the NBFC and the client.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must keep records of transactions for at least 10 years from the date of the transaction. This is to prevent money laundering and ensure compliance with regulations.
violation_message_template: Record preservation period violation: {transaction_id} exceeds the required 10-year preservation period.

title: Customer Identification Record Keeping
act_section: Rule 10 of PMLA Rules, 2005
source_clause: records pertaining to the identification of the customer and his address ... would continue to be preserved for at least ten years after the business relationship is ended
description: NBFCs and RNBCs must maintain customer identification records for at least 10 years after the business relationship ends
plain_english: This means: Banking companies must keep customer identification records for 10 years after the customer relationship ends. This is to help with potential investigations. If the records are not kept, it may hinder prosecution of criminal activity.
violation_message_template: Customer identification records for {customer_id} were not maintained for the required 10 years after the business relationship ended on {transaction_date}

title: UNSCR 1267 Compliance
source_clause: All NBFCs and RNBCs are accordingly advised to update the consolidated list of individuals/entities and before opening any new account, it should be ensured that the name/s of the proposed customer does not appear in the list
description: NBFCs and RNBCs must ensure that customers are not on the UNSCR 1267 list before opening new accounts
plain_english: This means: Banking companies must check if a customer is on the UNSCR 1267 list before opening a new account. If the customer is on the list, the account cannot be opened. This is to prevent transactions with terrorist individuals or organizations.
violation_message_template: Account {account_id} was opened for {customer_name}, who is listed on the UNSCR 1267 list on {transaction_date}

title: Terrorist List Update
source_clause: All NBFCs and RNBCs were advised to update the consolidated list of individuals/entities and also those consolidated list of individuals/entities, issued prior to above mentioned note.
description: NBFCs and RNBCs must update the list of terrorist individuals and organizations and check new and existing accounts against it.
plain_english: This means: Before opening a new account, NBFCs and RNBCs must check if the customer is on the terrorist list. They must also regularly scan existing accounts to ensure no account is held by or linked to any terrorist entity or individual.
violation_message_template: Account {account_id} of customer {customer_name} is linked to a terrorist entity or individual {entity_name} as per UNSCR 1267 (1999) and 1822(2008).

title: Scan Existing Accounts
act_section: Prevention of Money-laundering (Maintenance of Records of the Nature and Value of Transactions) Rules, 2005
source_clause: should scan all existing accounts to ensure that no account is held by or linked to any of the entities or individuals included in the list.
description: NBFCs and RNBCs must scan existing accounts to prevent money laundering.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs and RNBCs should regularly review their accounts to ensure they are not linked to entities or individuals on the list. This helps prevent money laundering. If an account is found to be linked, it must be reported.
violation_message_template: Account {account_id} held by {customer_name} is linked to a sanctioned entity.

title: AML CFT Deficient Jurisdictions
act_section: PMLA Rules 2005
source_clause: NBFCs and RNBCs were advised to strictly follow the amended provisions of PMLA Rules and ensure meticulous compliance to these Rules. All NBFCs/RNBCs were accordingly advised to take into account risks arising from the deficiencies in AML/CFT regime of these countries.
description: NBFCs and RNBCs must consider risks from AML/CFT deficient jurisdictions
plain_english: This means: NBFCs and RNBCs should be cautious when dealing with countries that have weak anti-money laundering and combating the financing of terrorism regulations, as they pose a risk to the international financial system. This includes countries like Iran, Angola, and Pakistan. NBFCs and RNBCs must take this into account when conducting business.
violation_message_template: Transaction with {country} detected, which is identified as an AML/CFT deficient jurisdiction.

title: AML CFT Risk Assessment
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
circular_reference: DNBS(PD).CC.No.172/03.10.42/2009-10 dated April 30, 2010 and DNBS(PD).CC.No209/03.10.42/2010-dated January 28, 2011
source_clause: All NBFCs (including RNBCs) were accordingly advised to take into account risks arising from the deficiencies in AML/CFT regime of these countries, while entering into business relationships and transactions with persons (including legal entities and other financial institutions) from or in these countries/ jurisdictions.
description: NBFCs must assess AML/CFT risks when dealing with certain countries. The countries include Iran, Democratic People's Republic of Korea, and others with strategic AML/CFT deficiencies.
plain_english: This means: When doing business with people or companies from certain countries, NBFCs must consider the risks of money laundering and terrorism financing. These countries have weaknesses in their systems to prevent such crimes.
violation_message_template: Transaction {transaction_id} from {country} exceeds risk threshold for AML/CFT deficiencies, requiring enhanced due diligence for {customer_name} on {transaction_date}.
condition_value: Iran, Democratic People's Republic of Korea, Angola, Ecuador, Ethiopia, Pakistan, Turkmenistan, Sao Tome and Principe

title: Enhanced Due Diligence
act_section: Section 45K and 45L of RBI Act,1934
source_clause: NBFCs were advised to apply enhanced due diligence measures on high risk customers. Some illustrative examples of customers requiring higher due diligence were also given in the paragraph under reference.
description: NBFCs are required to apply enhanced due diligence measures on high risk customers, including bullion dealers and jewelers.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must apply enhanced due diligence measures on high risk customers to prevent money laundering. This includes monitoring transactions and identifying suspicious activity. Failure to comply may result in penalties.
violation_message_template: NBFC {account_id} has failed to apply enhanced due diligence measures on high risk customer {customer_id} as required by RBI guidelines.

title: Ongoing Monitoring
act_section: Section 45K and 45L of RBI Act,1934
source_clause: Ongoing monitoring is an essential element of effective KYC procedures. It was advised that NBFCs are also required to subject these ‘high risk accounts’ to intensified transaction monitoring.
description: NBFCs are required to subject high risk accounts to ongoing monitoring and intensified transaction monitoring.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must continuously monitor high risk accounts and report suspicious transactions to FIU-ND to prevent money laundering. Failure to comply may result in penalties.
violation_message_template: NBFC {account_id} has failed to subject high risk account {customer_id} to ongoing monitoring and intensified transaction monitoring as required by RBI guidelines.

title: Suspicious Transaction Reporting
act_section: Section 45K and 45L of RBI Act,1934
source_clause: High risk associated with such accounts should be taken into account by NBFCs to identify suspicious transactions for filing Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) to FIU-ND.
description: NBFCs are required to identify and report suspicious transactions to FIU-ND.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must identify and report suspicious transactions from high risk accounts to FIU-ND to prevent money laundering. Failure to comply may result in penalties.
violation_message_template: NBFC {account_id} has failed to report suspicious transaction {transaction_id} from high risk account {customer_id} to FIU-ND as required by RBI guidelines.

title: High Risk Country Transaction
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: All NBFCs (including RNBCs) are accordingly advised to consider the information contained in the enclosed statement. All NBFCs (including RNBCs) are accordingly advised to take into account risks arising from the deficiencies in AML/CFT regime of these countries, while entering into business relationships and transactions with persons (including legal entities and other financial institutions) from or in these countries/ jurisdictions.
description: NBFCs and RNBCs must consider the risks associated with countries having strategic AML/CFT deficiencies. They should take into account these risks when entering into business relationships and transactions with persons from or in these countries.
plain_english: This means: When dealing with customers or entities from high-risk countries like Iran, Angola, and others, NBFCs and RNBCs must consider the increased risk of money laundering and terrorist financing. They should take extra precautions and apply countermeasures to protect the international financial system.
violation_message_template: Transaction with high-risk country {country} detected on {transaction_date} with amount {amount}.

title: Cash Transaction Reporting Threshold
act_section: Prevention of Money-laundering (Maintenance of Records of the Nature and Value of Transactions) Rules, 2005
source_clause: The debit transactions in the above example are integrally connected cash transactions because total cash debits during the calendar month exceeds Rs.10 lakhs.
description: NBFCs must report cash transactions exceeding Rs.10 lakhs in a calendar month. Only transactions above Rs.50,000 should be reported separately.
plain_english: This means: If the total cash debits in a month exceed Rs.10 lakhs, the NBFC must report these transactions. However, only transactions above Rs.50,000 should be reported separately. This helps prevent money laundering.
violation_message_template: Cash transaction of {amount} on {transaction_date} exceeds the threshold of Rs.10 lakhs for the month, but is below the separate reporting threshold of Rs.50,000.

title: Credit Transaction Reporting
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: All the credit transactions in the above example would not be treated as integrally connected, as the sum total of the credit transactions during the month does not exceed Rs.10 lakh and hence credit transaction dated 02, 07 & 08/04/2008 should not be reported by NBFC.
description: NBFCs are not required to report credit transactions if the total monthly amount does not exceed Rs.10 lakh.
plain_english: This means: If the total credit transactions in a month are less than or equal to Rs.10 lakh, NBFCs should not report these transactions. This applies to all credit transactions that are not integrally connected.
violation_message_template: Credit transaction {transaction_id} on {transaction_date} with amount {amount} was not reported, but the total monthly credit transactions exceeded the threshold of {threshold_value}.

title: Suspicious Cash Transactions
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Company transactions, that are denominated by unusually large amounts of cash, rather than normally associated with the normal commercial operations of the company, e.g. cheques, Transactions that do not make Economic Sense
description: The company should report transactions involving large amounts of cash that are not consistent with normal commercial operations, as well as transactions that do not make economic sense.
plain_english: This means: Companies must report suspicious transactions involving large amounts of cash that are unusual for their business, or transactions that don't make economic sense, to prevent money laundering.
violation_message_template: Suspicious transaction detected: {transaction_id} on {transaction_date} with {amount} in cash, which is unusual for {customer_name}'s business operations.

title: Suspicious Activity Reporting
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Activities not consistent with the Customer's Business or Accounts with large volume of credits whereas the nature of business does not justify such credits.
description: NBFCs must monitor and report suspicious activities, including those that are inconsistent with a customer's business or involve large volumes of credits that are not justified by the business.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must identify and report suspicious transactions that do not align with a customer's business profile. This includes large cash transactions or multiple accounts under the same name. If a customer's activities seem unusual, the NBFC must report it.
violation_message_template: Suspicious activity detected for {customer_name} with {account_id} on {transaction_date} with {transaction_type} of {amount}

title: Customer Information Requirements
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: A customer who is reluctant to provide information needed for a mandatory report, to have the report filed or to proceed with a transaction after being informed that the report must be filed.
description: NBFCs must obtain complete information from customers, including the purpose of their business and financial statements.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must collect and verify customer information, including business purpose and financial statements, to ensure compliance with reporting requirements. If a customer is reluctant to provide this information, it may indicate suspicious activity.
violation_message_template: Customer {customer_name} with {account_id} failed to provide required information on {transaction_date}

title: Employee Conduct Monitoring
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: An employee whose lavish lifestyle cannot be supported by his or her salary.
description: NBFCs must monitor employee conduct and report suspicious behavior, including lavish lifestyles that cannot be supported by their salary.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must keep an eye on employee behavior and report any suspicious activity, such as employees living beyond their means. This helps prevent internal fraud and ensures a safe working environment.
violation_message_template: Employee {employee_name} with {employee_id} has a suspicious lifestyle that cannot be supported by their salary

title: Anonymous Account Opening
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: No account is opened in anonymous or fictitious/ benami name(s);
description: Banks are prohibited from opening accounts in anonymous or fictitious names.
plain_english: This means: Banks must not open accounts in names that are not genuine or are fictitious. This is to prevent money laundering and other illegal activities. If a bank opens such an account, it may face penalties.
violation_message_template: Account {account_id} was opened in an anonymous or fictitious name {customer_name} on {transaction_date}, which is a violation of KYC norms.

title: KYC Policy Framework
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: All NBFCs are, therefore, advised to adopt the same with suitable modifications depending on the activity undertaken by them and ensure that a proper policy framework on ‘Know Your Customer’ and Anti-Money Laundering measures is formulated and put in place with the approval of the Board within three months of the date of this circular.
description: NBFCs must formulate a KYC policy framework
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must create a policy framework for Know Your Customer and Anti-Money Laundering within three months.

title: Confidentiality of Customer Information
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: While preparing operational guidelines NBFCs may bear in mind that the information collected from the customer for the purpose of opening of account should be kept as confidential and not divulge any details thereof for cross selling or any other purposes.
description: NBFCs must keep customer information confidential
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must keep customer information confidential and not use it for cross-selling or other purposes.

title: KYC Guidelines for Authorized Persons
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Adherence to Know Your Customer (KYC) guidelines by NBFC and persons authorised by NBFCs including brokers/agents etc.
description: KYC guidelines apply to authorized persons
plain_english: This means: KYC guidelines must be followed by NBFCs and their authorized persons, including brokers and agents.

title: KYC Compliance for NBFCs
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: The NBFC should make available all information to the Bank to verify the compliance with the KYC guidelines and accept full consequences of any violation by the persons authorised by NBFCs including brokers/agents etc. who are operating on its behalf.
description: NBFCs must ensure KYC compliance for authorized persons.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must provide information to the Bank to verify that authorized persons, such as brokers or agents, are following KYC guidelines. NBFCs are responsible for any violations by these authorized persons.

title: KYC Compliance for RNBCs
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: The RNBC should make available all information to the regulator or his nominee to verify the compliance with the KYC guidelines and accept full consequences of any violation by the agent / sub-agent who is operating on its behalf.
description: RNBCs must ensure KYC compliance for agents and sub-agents.
plain_english: This means: RNBCs must provide information to the regulator to verify that agents and sub-agents are following KYC guidelines. RNBCs are responsible for any violations by these agents and sub-agents.

title: KYC for Existing RNBC Customers
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: For the existing customers, initially, KYC guidelines should be complied in respect of large customers whose aggregate deposit exceeds Rs.1 lakh.
description: RNBCs must apply KYC guidelines to existing large customers.
plain_english: This means: For RNBCs, KYC guidelines must be applied to existing customers with deposits over Rs.1 lakh. For other existing customers, KYC details should be updated at deposit renewal time.

title: NBFC Deposit Receipt Requirements
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: All deposit receipts should bear the name and Registered Office address of the NBFC and must invariably indicate the name of the persons authorised by NBFCs including brokers/agents etc. and their addresses who mobilised the deposit and the link office with the telephone number of such officer and/or persons authorised by NBFCs including brokers/agents etc.
description: NBFCs must ensure deposit receipts include specific details for customer identification and contact.
plain_english: This means: All deposit receipts must have the NBFC's name and address, and include details of the person who collected the deposit, so customers can easily contact them.
violation_message_template: Deposit receipt {receipt_id} for {customer_name} does not contain required details.

title: NBFC Customer Service Requirements
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: The companies may also evolve suitable review procedures to identify persons authorised by NBFCs including brokers/agents etc. in whose cases the incidence of discontinued deposits is high for taking suitable action.
description: NBFCs should have procedures to review and address issues with agents or brokers who have high rates of discontinued deposits.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs should regularly review the performance of their agents and brokers, and take action if many deposits are discontinued.
violation_message_template: No procedures in place for reviewing {agent_name}'s performance.

title: Simplified KYC for Low Balance Accounts
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs may open accounts for persons who intend to keep balances not exceeding rupees fifty thousand (Rs. 50,000/-) in all their accounts taken together and the total credit in all the accounts taken together is not expected to exceed rupees one lakh (Rs. 1,00,000/-) in a year, subject to introduction from another account holder who has been subjected to full KYC procedure or any other evidence as to the identity and address of the customer to the satisfaction of the NBFC.
description: NBFCs can open accounts with simplified KYC for customers with low balances, provided they meet certain conditions.
plain_english: This means: If a customer wants to open an account with a balance of Rs. 50,000 or less and total credit of Rs. 1,00,000 or less per year, the NBFC can open the account with a simpler KYC process. The customer must either be introduced by an existing account holder who has completed the full KYC process or provide other evidence of identity and address.
violation_message_template: The account {account_id} for customer {customer_name} has exceeded the balance threshold of {threshold_value} or total credit of {threshold_value} in a year without completing the full KYC procedure.

title: Notification for KYC Documents
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: The NBFC must notify the customer when the balance reaches rupees forty thousand (Rs. 40,000/-) or the total credit in a year reaches rupees eighty thousand (Rs. 80,000/-) that appropriate documents for conducting the KYC must be submitted.
description: NBFCs are required to notify customers when their account balances reach certain thresholds, requiring them to submit KYC documents.
plain_english: This means: If a customer's account balance reaches Rs. 40,000 or total credit reaches Rs. 80,000 in a year, the NBFC must remind them to submit KYC documents. If the customer doesn't, and the balance exceeds Rs. 50,000 or total credit exceeds Rs. 1,00,000, no further transactions will be allowed.
violation_message_template: The customer {customer_name} with account {account_id} has not submitted KYC documents after being notified that their balance of {balance} or total credit of {total_credit} requires them to do so.

title: KYC Documentation for Customer Identification
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs are advised to take a review of their extant internal instructions in this regard. It may happen that Annex-VIII, which was clearly termed as an indicative list, may be treated by some NBFCs as an exhaustive list as a result of which a section of public may be denied access to financial services.
description: NBFCs must review internal instructions for customer identification to ensure they are not treating the indicative list in Annex-VIII as exhaustive.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs should check their current rules for identifying customers to make sure they are not unfairly denying services to anyone. They should not consider the list in Annex-VIII as the only acceptable documents.

title: Verification of Customer Address
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: In case utility bill is not in the name of person depositing money but is close relative wife, son, daughter and parents etc. who live with their husband, father/mother and son, NBFCs can obtain an identity document and a utility bill of the relative with whom the prospective customer is living along with a declaration from the relative that the said person (prospective customer) wanting to open an account is a relative and is staying with him/her.
description: NBFCs can verify a customer's address through a relative's utility bill and declaration.
plain_english: This means: If a utility bill is not in the customer's name but in a close relative's name, NBFCs can still use it for address verification if they get a declaration from the relative confirming the customer's address.

title: Periodic Review of Risk Categorization
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs are required to put in place a system of periodical review of risk categorisation of accounts and the need for applying enhanced due diligence measures in case of higher risk perception on a customer. NBFCs are further advised that such review of risk categorisation of customers should be carried out at a periodicity of not less than once in six months.
description: NBFCs must review risk categorization of customers periodically.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must review the risk level of their customers at least once every six months. They also need to update customer identification data regularly.

title: Updation of Customer Identification Data
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: The periodicity of such updation should not be less than once in five years in case of low risk category customers and not less than once in two years in case of high and medium risk categories.
description: NBFCs must update customer identification data periodically based on risk category.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must update customer identification data at least once every 5 years for low-risk customers and at least once every 2 years for high and medium-risk customers.

title: KYC/AML Guidelines for Overseas Branches
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: KYC/AML guidelines issued by Reserve Bank of India shall also apply to their branches and majority owned subsidiaries located outside India, especially, in countries which do not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations, to the extent local laws permit.
description: NBFCs must apply KYC/AML guidelines to overseas branches.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must follow RBI's KYC/AML guidelines for their overseas branches and subsidiaries, if allowed by local laws.

title: Reporting of Suspicious Transactions
act_section: PMLA Rules
source_clause: NBFCs are advised to develop suitable mechanism through appropriate policy framework for enhanced monitoring of accounts suspected of having terrorist links and swift identification of the transactions and making suitable reports to the Financial Intelligence Unit – India (FIU-IND) on priority.
description: NBFCs must report suspicious transactions to FIU-IND.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must have a system to monitor accounts that may be linked to terrorism and report suspicious transactions to FIU-IND quickly.

title: Screening for UN Sanctions List
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs should ensure to update the consolidated list of individuals and entities as circulated by Reserve Bank. NBFCs are advised that before opening any new account it should be ensured that the name/s of the proposed customer does not appear in the list.
description: NBFCs must update and check the UN sanctions list before opening new accounts.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must check if a customer's name is on the UN sanctions list before opening a new account. They must also update their list of sanctioned individuals and entities.
violation_message_template: The customer {customer_name} has been identified as being on the UN sanctions list, but their account was opened on {date}.

title: Screening Mechanism for Recruitment
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: It would, therefore, be necessary that adequate screening mechanism is put in place by NBFCs as an integral part of their recruitment/hiring process of personnel.
description: NBFCs must have a screening mechanism in place for recruitment.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must have a system to check the background of new employees.
violation_message_template: The NBFC {NBFC_name} did not have a proper screening mechanism in place for recruitment, leading to the hiring of {employee_name} on {date}.

title: Suspicious Transaction Alerts
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs may consider the indicative list of suspicious activities contained in Annex-V of the CC No.126 dated August 05, 2008.
description: NBFCs should consider using an indicative list of suspicious activities.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs can use a list of suspicious activities to generate alerts.
violation_message_template: The NBFC {NBFC_name} failed to implement an effective system to generate alerts for suspicious transactions on {date}.

title: Suspicion of Money Laundering/Terrorist Financing
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: whenever there is suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing or when other factors give rise to a belief that the customer does not, in fact, pose a low risk, NBFCs were advised to carry out full scale customer due diligence (CDD) before opening an account.
description: NBFCs must carry out full customer due diligence when suspicious of money laundering or terrorist financing.
plain_english: This means: If a NBFC suspects money laundering or terrorist financing, they must do a full check on the customer before opening an account.
violation_message_template: The NBFC {name} failed to conduct full customer due diligence for {customer_name} with suspicious transaction {transaction_id}.

title: Filing of Suspicious Transaction Report (STR)
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: in the circumstances when a NBFC believes that it would no longer be satisfied that it knows the true identity of the account holder, the Company should also file an STR with FIU-IND.
description: NBFCs must file a Suspicious Transaction Report when unable to verify a customer's identity.
plain_english: This means: If a NBFC can't verify a customer's identity, they must report it to FIU-IND.
violation_message_template: The NBFC {name} failed to file STR for {customer_name} with unverified identity.

title: Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) Approval
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: In the event of an existing customer or the beneficial owner of an existing account, subsequently becoming a PEP, NBFCs (including RNBCS) were advised to obtain senior management approval to continue the business relationship and subject the account to the CDD measures as applicable to the customers of PEP
description: NBFCs must obtain senior management approval to continue business with a customer who becomes a PEP.
plain_english: This means: If a customer becomes a Politically Exposed Person, the NBFC must get senior management approval to keep doing business with them.
violation_message_template: The NBFC {name} failed to obtain senior management approval for {customer_name} who became a PEP.

title: Identification of Beneficial Owners
