act_section: Section 45K and 45L of Reserve Bank of India Regulation Act, 1934
source_clause: beneficial owners must be identified. Where such funds are co-mingled at the NBFC, the NBFC should still look through to the beneficial owners.
description: NBFCs are required to identify beneficial owners of accounts.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must find out who the real owners of an account are, even if the account is held by a professional intermediary like a lawyer or chartered accountant.
violation_message_template: The NBFC {name} failed to identify the beneficial owner of account {account_id} held by {customer_name}.

title: Prohibition on Accounts by Professional Intermediaries
act_section: Section 45K and 45L of Reserve Bank of India Regulation Act, 1934
source_clause: NBFCs should not allow opening and/or holding of an account on behalf of a client/s by professional intermediaries, like Lawyers and Chartered Accountants, etc., who are unable to disclose true identity of the owner of the account/funds due to any professional obligation of customer confidentiality.
description: NBFCs are prohibited from allowing professional intermediaries to hold accounts on behalf of clients if it prevents identification of the beneficial owner.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must not allow lawyers, chartered accountants, or similar professionals to open or hold accounts for clients if they cannot reveal the true owner due to confidentiality obligations.
violation_message_template: The NBFC {name} allowed a professional intermediary {intermediary_name} to hold an account {account_id} on behalf of client {customer_name} without disclosing the beneficial owner.

title: Transactions with High-Risk Countries
act_section: Section 45K and 45L of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
source_clause: NBFCs should give special attention to business relationships and transactions with persons (including legal persons and other financial institutions) from or in countries which do not or insufficiently apply the FATF recommendations.
description: NBFCs must scrutinize transactions with entities from countries with AML/CFT deficiencies.
plain_english: This means: When dealing with businesses or individuals from countries that do not follow FATF recommendations, NBFCs must be extra careful and check the purpose of transactions. If a transaction seems suspicious or has no clear reason, NBFCs must investigate and keep records.
violation_message_template: Transaction with high-risk country {country} from {customer_name} ({customer_id}) has no apparent economic or visible lawful purpose.

title: Ongoing Monitoring of Transactions
act_section: Section 45K and 45L of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
source_clause: It is advised that NBFCs should examine the background and purpose of transactions with persons (including legal persons and other financial institutions) from jurisdictions included in FATF Statements and countries that do not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations.
description: NBFCs must continuously monitor transactions with high-risk jurisdictions.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must regularly check the background and purpose of transactions with businesses or individuals from countries that do not follow FATF recommendations.
violation_message_template: No records of transaction monitoring with high-risk country {country} from {customer_name} ({customer_id}).

title: High-Risk Countries for AML/CFT
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: All NBFCs/RNBCs were accordingly advised to take into account risks arising from the deficiencies in AML/CFT regime of these countries.
description: NBFCs/RNBCs must consider risks from countries with AML/CFT deficiencies.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs and RNBCs should be cautious when dealing with countries that have weaknesses in their anti-money laundering and combating the financing of terrorism systems.

title: FATF Statement on AML/CFT Deficiencies
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: All NBFCs/RNBCs were accordingly advised to consider the information contained in the enclosed statement.
description: NBFCs/RNBCs must consider FATF's statement on AML/CFT deficiencies.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs and RNBCs should take into account the information provided by the Financial Action Task Force regarding countries with AML/CFT deficiencies.

title: KYC/AML/CFT Guidelines for NBFCs
act_section: Section 12 of PMLA 2002
source_clause: NBFCs were advised to strictly adhere to the guidelines on KYC/AML/CFT issued from time to time and to those relating to periodical updation of customer identification data after the account is opened and also to monitoring of transactions in order to protect themselves and their customers from misuse by such fraudsters.
description: NBFCs must adhere to KYC/AML/CFT guidelines and monitor transactions to prevent money laundering.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must follow rules to know their customers and prevent money laundering. They must update customer information and monitor transactions to prevent fraud.
violation_message_template: NBFC {name} failed to adhere to KYC/AML/CFT guidelines for customer {customer_name}

title: Reporting of Suspicious Transactions
act_section: Section 12 of PMLA 2002
source_clause: NBFCs were advised to appoint a Principal Officer and put in place a system of internal reporting of suspicious transactions and cash transactions of Rs.10 lakh and above.
description: NBFCs must report suspicious transactions and cash transactions above Rs.10 lakh.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must have a system to report suspicious transactions and cash transactions over Rs.10 lakh to prevent money laundering.
violation_message_template: NBFC {name} failed to report suspicious transaction {transaction_id} of {amount}

title: Cash Transaction Reporting Threshold
act_section: Section 12 of PMLA 2002
source_clause: NBFCs should introduce a system of maintaining proper record of transactions prescribed under Rule 3, as mentioned below: all cash transactions of the value of more than rupees ten lakh or its equivalent in foreign currency;
description: NBFCs must record cash transactions over Rs. 10 lakh
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must keep a record of all cash transactions that are more than Rs. 10 lakh or its equivalent in foreign currency. They must also record suspicious transactions.
violation_message_template: Transaction {transaction_id} of {amount} on {transaction_date} was not recorded

title: Aggregated Cash Transaction Reporting Threshold
act_section: Section 12 of PMLA 2002
source_clause: all series of cash transactions integrally connected to each other which have been valued below rupees ten lakh or its equivalent in foreign currency where such series of transactions have taken place within a month and the aggregate value of such transactions exceeds rupees ten lakh;
description: NBFCs must record aggregated cash transactions over Rs. 10 lakh within a month
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must keep a record of a series of cash transactions that are below Rs. 10 lakh each but add up to more than Rs. 10 lakh within a month.
violation_message_template: Transactions {transaction_id} of {amount} on {transaction_date} aggregated over {days_overdue} days exceeded {threshold_value}

title: Suspicious Transaction Reporting
act_section: Section 12 of PMLA 2002
source_clause: all suspicious transactions whether or not made in cash and in manner as mentioned in the Rules framed by Government of India under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002.
description: NBFCs must report suspicious transactions
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must report all suspicious transactions, whether in cash or not, as per the Rules framed by the Government of India under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002.
violation_message_template: Suspicious transaction {transaction_id} on {transaction_date} was not reported

title: Record Keeping Requirements
act_section: Section 12 of PMLA 2002
source_clause: NBFCs should take appropriate steps to evolve a system for proper maintenance and preservation of account information in a manner that allows data to be retrieved easily and quickly whenever required or when requested by the competent authorities.
description: NBFCs must maintain and preserve account information
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must have a system to properly maintain and preserve account information so that it can be easily retrieved when needed or requested by competent authorities.
violation_message_template: Account information for {customer_id} was not properly maintained

title: Record Retention Period
act_section: Section 12 of PMLA 2002
source_clause: NBFCs should maintain for at least ten years from the date of cessation of transaction between the NBFCs and the client, all necessary records of
description: NBFCs must retain records for at least 10 years
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must keep all necessary records for at least 10 years from the date the transaction with the client ended.
violation_message_template: Records for {customer_id} were not retained for {record_age_years} years

title: Record Keeping for Customer Identification
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs should ensure that records pertaining to the identification of the customer and his address (e.g. copies of documents like passports, identity cards, driving licenses, PAN, utility bills etc.) obtained while opening the account and during the course of business relationship, are properly preserved for at least ten years after the business relationship is ended.
description: NBFCs must keep customer identification records for 10 years
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must keep records of customer identification and address for at least 10 years after the business relationship ends. These records must be made available to competent authorities upon request.
violation_message_template: NBFC failed to preserve customer identification records for {customer_id} for {record_age_years} years

title: Reporting to Financial Intelligence Unit-India
act_section: PMLA rules
source_clause: NBFCs are required to report information relating to cash and suspicious transactions to the Director, Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND)
description: NBFCs must report cash and suspicious transactions to FIU-IND
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must report cash and suspicious transactions to the Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND) in the prescribed formats.
violation_message_template: NBFC failed to report {transaction_type} transaction to FIU-IND for {customer_id}

title: Transaction Monitoring Mechanism
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs, as a part of transaction monitoring mechanism, are required to put in place an appropriate software application to throw alerts when the transactions are inconsistent with risk categorization and updated profile of customers.
description: NBFCs must implement a transaction monitoring mechanism with software that throws alerts for transactions inconsistent with customer risk categorization.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must use software to monitor transactions and alert when they don't match the customer's risk profile. This helps identify suspicious transactions.
violation_message_template: NBFC {name} failed to implement transaction monitoring mechanism for customer {customer_id}

title: Electronic Filing of Reports
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs were advised to initiate urgent steps to ensure electronic filing of cash transaction report (CTR) and Suspicious Transaction Reports (STR) to FIU-IND.
description: NBFCs must electronically file CTR and STR reports to FIU-IND.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must urgently start filing cash transaction and suspicious transaction reports electronically with FIU-IND.
violation_message_template: NBFC {name} failed to electronically file CTR/STR reports to FIU-IND for transaction {transaction_id}

title: Cash Transaction Reporting Threshold
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: The cut-off limit of Rupees ten lakh is applicable to integrally connected cash transactions also.
description: NBFCs must report cash transactions exceeding Rs. 10 lakh to FIU-IND.
plain_english: This means: If cash transactions exceed Rs. 10 lakh in a month, NBFCs must report them to FIU-IND. The threshold applies to integrally connected transactions.
violation_message_template: NBFC {name} failed to report cash transaction exceeding Rs. {threshold_value} to FIU-IND on {transaction_date}.

title: CTR Submission Frequency
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: cash transaction reporting by branches/offices of NBFCs to their Principal Officer should invariably be submitted on monthly basis
description: NBFCs must submit CTR to Principal Officer on a monthly basis.
plain_english: This means: NBFC branches/offices must submit CTR to their Principal Officer every month.
violation_message_template: NBFC {name} failed to submit CTR to Principal Officer on a monthly basis for {month}.

title: CTR Exclusion Limit
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: while filing CTR, details of individual cash transactions below rupees fifty thousand may not be indicated
description: NBFCs are not required to report individual cash transactions below Rs. 50,000.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs do not need to report cash transactions below Rs. 50,000 to FIU-IND.

title: Counterfeit Currency Reporting
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Counterfeit Currency Report – CCR as per Annex-II should be reported by the Principal Officer to FIU-IND immediately.
description: NBFCs must report counterfeit currency transactions to FIU-IND immediately.
plain_english: This means: If a NBFC finds counterfeit currency has been used as genuine, they must report it to FIU-IND right away.
violation_message_template: Counterfeit currency transaction reported to FIU-IND with {transaction_id} on {transaction_date}

title: Record Keeping for Unusual Transactions
act_section: PMLA, 2002
source_clause: These records are required to be preserved for ten years as is required under PMLA, 2002.
description: NBFCs must keep records of unusual transactions for 10 years.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must keep records of complex or unusual transactions for 10 years.
violation_message_template: Records of unusual transactions not preserved for {record_age_years} years

title: Reporting Attempted Suspicious Transactions
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs should report all such attempted transactions in STRs, even if not completed by customers, irrespective of the amount of the transaction.
description: NBFCs must report attempted suspicious transactions to FIU-IND.
plain_english: This means: If a customer tries to make a suspicious transaction but doesn't complete it, the NBFC must still report it.
violation_message_template: Attempted suspicious transaction not reported to FIU-IND with {transaction_id} on {transaction_date}

title: Definition of Suspicious Transaction
act_section: Rule 2(g) of PMLA Rules
source_clause: NBFCs should make STRs if they have reasonable ground to believe that the transaction involve proceeds of crime generally irrespective of the amount of transaction.
description: NBFCs must report transactions suspected to involve crime proceeds.
plain_english: This means: If a NBFC thinks a transaction might involve money from crime, they must report it, no matter the amount.
violation_message_template: Suspicious transaction not reported to FIU-IND with {transaction_id} on {transaction_date}

title: Record Retention Period
act_section: Rule 10 of PMLA Rules 2005
source_clause: records pertaining to the identification of the customer and his address... would continue to be preserved for at least ten years after the business relationship is ended
description: Records of customer identification and address must be kept for 10 years after the business relationship ends
plain_english: This means: Financial institutions must keep customer identification records for at least 10 years after the customer relationship ends. These records include copies of documents like passports, identity cards, and utility bills.
violation_message_template: Records of customer {customer_name} not retained for required 10 years after business relationship ended on {date}

title: Terrorist List Verification
source_clause: All NBFCs and RNBCs are advised to update the consolidated list of individuals/entities and before opening any new account, it should be ensured that the name/s of the proposed customer does not appear in the list
description: Financial institutions must verify customers against UNSCR 1267 list before opening an account
plain_english: This means: Before opening a new account, financial institutions must check if the customer's name is on the UNSCR 1267 list of terrorist individuals and organizations. They must also update and review existing accounts against this list.
violation_message_template: New account opened for {customer_name} without verifying against UNSCR 1267 list on {date}

title: UNSC 1267 List Check for New Accounts
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Before opening any new account, it should be ensured that the name/s of the proposed customer does not appear in the list of individuals/entities linked to Al-Qaida and Taliban under UNSCR 1267 (1999) and 1822(2008).
description: NBFCs and RNBCs must check new customers against the UNSC 1267 list.
plain_english: This means: Before opening a new account, the bank must check if the customer's name is on the UNSC 1267 list of terrorist individuals and organizations. If the customer is on the list, the bank should not open the account.
violation_message_template: The customer {customer_name} is on the UNSC 1267 list, but account {account_id} was opened on {transaction_date}.

title: UNSC 1267 List Check for Existing Accounts
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs and RNBCs were advised to scan all existing accounts to ensure that no account is held by or linked to any of the entities or individuals included in the list of individuals/entities linked to Al-Qaida and Taliban under UNSCR 1267 (1999) and 1822(2008).
description: NBFCs and RNBCs must review existing accounts against the UNSC 1267 list.
plain_english: This means: The bank must review all existing accounts to ensure none are held by individuals or entities on the UNSC 1267 list. If an account is found, the bank must take action.
violation_message_template: The account {account_id} is held by {customer_name} who is on the UNSC 1267 list, but was not flagged on {flag_date}.

title: Scanning Accounts Against Sanctions List
act_section: Prevention of Money-laundering (Maintenance of Records of the Nature and Value of Transactions, the Procedure and Manner of Maintaining and Time for Furnishing Information and Verification and Maintenance of Records of the Identity of the Clients of the Banking Companies, Financial Institutions and Intermediaries) Amendment Rules, 2009
source_clause: NBFCs and RNBCs are advised to scan all existing accounts to ensure that no account is held by or linked to any of the entities or individuals included in the list.
description: NBFCs and RNBCs must scan existing accounts against sanctions lists.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs and RNBCs must check all their current accounts to ensure none belong to individuals or entities on sanctions lists. They must take action to prevent accounts of sanctioned parties.
violation_message_template: Account {account_id} of {customer_name} found to be linked to sanctioned entity {entity_name}

title: Compliance with PMLA Rules
act_section: Prevention of Money-laundering (Maintenance of Records of the Nature and Value of Transactions, the Procedure and Manner of Maintaining and Time for Furnishing Information and Verification and Maintenance of Records of the Identity of the Clients of the Banking Companies, Financial Institutions and Intermediaries) Amendment Rules, 2009
source_clause: NBFCs and RNBCs are advised to strictly follow the amended provisions of PMLA Rules and ensure meticulous compliance to these Rules.
description: NBFCs and RNBCs must comply with PMLA Rules.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs and RNBCs must follow and fully comply with the updated PMLA Rules to prevent money laundering.
violation_message_template: Non-compliance with PMLA Rules detected in {account_id}

title: AML/CFT Risk Assessment for Specific Jurisdictions
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: All NBFCs/RNBCs were accordingly advised to take into account risks arising from the deficiencies in AML/CFT regime of these countries.
description: NBFCs and RNBCs must consider AML/CFT risks associated with specific jurisdictions.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs and RNBCs should be aware of the money laundering and terrorist financing risks in certain countries and take them into account.

title: Enhanced Due Diligence for High Risk Customers
act_section: Section 45K and 45L of RBI Act, 1934 read with Rule 7 of Prevention of Money-laundering (Maintenance of Records of the Nature and Value of Transactions, the Procedure and Manner of Maintaining and Time for Furnishing Information and Verification and Maintenance of Records of the Identity of the Clients of the Banking Companies, Financial Institutions and Intermediaries) Rules, 2005
source_clause: All NBFCs (including RNBCs) were advised to take note of modifications to the circular No 184, dated July 01, 2010 as under: NBFCs were advised to apply enhanced due diligence measures on high risk customers.
description: NBFCs are required to apply enhanced due diligence measures on high-risk customers.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must perform extra checks on customers who are considered high-risk. These checks help prevent money laundering and terrorist financing.

title: Categorization of Bullion Dealers and Jewelers as High Risk
act_section: Section 45K and 45L of RBI Act, 1934 read with Rule 7 of Prevention of Money-laundering (Maintenance of Records of the Nature and Value of Transactions, the Procedure and Manner of Maintaining and Time for Furnishing Information and Verification and Maintenance of Records of the Identity of the Clients of the Banking Companies, Financial Institutions and Intermediaries) Rules, 2005
source_clause: NBFCs were further advised that in view of the risks involved in cash intensive businesses, accounts of bullion dealers(including sub-dealers) and jewelers should also be categorized by NBFCs as ‘high risk’ requiring enhanced due diligence.
description: Bullion dealers and jewelers must be categorized as high-risk customers by NBFCs.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must consider bullion dealers and jewelers as high-risk customers and perform extra checks on them.

title: Ongoing Monitoring of High Risk Accounts
act_section: Section 45K and 45L of RBI Act, 1934 read with Rule 7 of Prevention of Money-laundering (Maintenance of Records of the Nature and Value of Transactions, the Procedure and Manner of Maintaining and Time for Furnishing Information and Verification and Maintenance of Records of the Identity of the Clients of the Banking Companies, Financial Institutions and Intermediaries) Rules, 2005
source_clause: Ongoing monitoring is an essential element of effective KYC procedures. It was advised that NBFCs are also required to subject these ‘high risk accounts’ to intensified transaction monitoring.
description: NBFCs must perform ongoing monitoring of high-risk accounts.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must regularly review transactions of high-risk customers to detect suspicious activity.

title: Consider FATF AML/CFT Deficiency Information
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: All NBFCs/RNBCs are accordingly advised to consider the information contained in the enclosed statement.
description: NBFCs/RNBCs must consider FATF's AML/CFT deficiency information.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs and RNBCs should take into account the information provided by FATF regarding jurisdictions with strategic AML/CFT deficiencies.

title: Apply Countermeasures for High-Risk Countries
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: All NBFCs (including RNBCs) are accordingly advised to take into account risks arising from the deficiencies in AML/CFT regime of these countries, while entering into business relationships and transactions with persons (including legal entities and other financial institutions) from or in these countries/ jurisdictions.
description: NBFCs/RNBCs must apply countermeasures for high-risk countries.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs and RNBCs should consider the risks associated with countries having AML/CFT deficiencies when dealing with them.

title: Suspicious Transaction Indicators
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Accounts with large volume of credits whereas the nature of business does not justify such credits. Attempts to avoid Reporting/Record-keeping Requirements (i) A customer who is reluctant to provide information needed for a mandatory report, to have the report filed or to proceed with a transaction after being informed that the report must be filed.
description: The NBFC should monitor for accounts and transactions that indicate suspicious activity, such as large credits not justified by the customer's business, attempts to avoid reporting or record-keeping requirements, and customer reluctance to provide necessary information.
plain_english: This means: The NBFC should watch out for transactions or accounts that seem unusual or suspicious, such as large credits that don't match the customer's business, or customers who don't want to provide required information. If a customer is hesitant to provide information for a mandatory report or proceed with a transaction after being told a report must be filed, it may indicate suspicious activity.
violation_message_template: The customer {customer_name} has shown reluctance to provide information needed for a mandatory report, indicating potential suspicious activity.

title: Suspicious Customer Behavior
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: (i) A customer/company who is reluctant to provide complete information regarding the purpose of the business, prior business relationships, officers or directors, or its locations. (ii) A customer/company who is reluctant to reveal details about its activities or to provide financial statements.
description: The NBFC should be cautious of customers who are reluctant to provide complete information about their business, activities, or financial statements.
plain_english: This means: If a customer doesn't want to give full information about their business, activities, or financial statements, it may indicate suspicious behavior.
violation_message_template: The customer {customer_name} has been reluctant to provide complete information regarding their business purpose or activities.

title: Employee Suspicious Behavior
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: (i) An employee whose lavish lifestyle cannot be supported by his or her salary. (ii) Negligence of employees/willful blindness is reported repeatedly.
description: The NBFC should monitor employee behavior for signs of suspicious activity, such as a lavish lifestyle not supported by salary or repeated negligence.
plain_english: This means: If an employee's lifestyle seems too good to be supported by their salary, or if they show repeated negligence, it may indicate suspicious behavior.
violation_message_template: The employee {employee_name} shows signs of suspicious behavior, such as a lavish lifestyle not supported by their salary.

title: Customer Acceptance Policy
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Banks should develop a clear Customer Acceptance Policy laying down explicit criteria for acceptance of customers.
description: Banks must have a clear policy for accepting customers.
plain_english: This means: Banks must have a clear policy on who they will accept as customers.

title: No Anonymous Accounts
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: No account is opened in anonymous or fictitious/ benami name(s);
description: Banks are prohibited from opening accounts in anonymous or fictitious names.
plain_english: This means: Banks cannot open accounts in fake or anonymous names.

title: Customer Risk Categorization
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Parameters of risk perception are clearly defined in terms of the nature of business activity, location of customer and his clients, mode of payments, volume of turnover, social and financial status etc. to enable categorization of customers into low, medium and high risk.
description: Banks must categorize customers into low, medium, and high risk based on defined parameters.
plain_english: This means: Banks must assess customer risk using factors like business activity, location, payment methods, and financial status. They must classify customers as low, medium, or high risk.

title: Documentation Requirements
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Documentation requirements and other information to be collected in respect of different categories of customers depending on perceived risk and keeping in mind the requirements of PML Act, 2002 and guidelines issued by Reserve Bank from time to time;
description: Banks must collect documentation and information based on customer risk category and PML Act requirements.
plain_english: This means: Banks must gather necessary documents and information from customers based on their risk category and the PML Act requirements.

title: Account Opening and Closure
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Not to open an account or close an existing account where the bank is unable to apply appropriate customer due diligence measures i.e. bank is unable to verify the identity and /or obtain documents required as per the risk categorisation due to non cooperation of the customer or non reliability of the data/information furnished to the bank.
description: Banks must not open or close accounts if they cannot apply due diligence measures.
plain_english: This means: Banks must not open a new account or close an existing one if they cannot properly verify the customer's identity or obtain required documents due to customer non-cooperation or unreliable information.

title: Customer Due Diligence for Representative
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Circumstances, in which a customer is permitted to act on behalf of another person/entity, should be clearly spelt out in conformity with the established law and practice of banking.
description: Banks must clearly outline circumstances for customers acting on behalf of others.
plain_english: This means: Banks must clearly define when a customer can act on behalf of another person or entity, following established banking laws and practices.

title: Checking Customer Background
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Necessary checks before opening a new account so as to ensure that the identity of the customer does not match with any person with known criminal background or with banned entities such as individual terrorists or terrorist organizations etc.
description: Banks must check new customers' backgrounds to ensure they are not criminals or banned entities.
plain_english: This means: Before opening a new account, banks must check that the customer is not a known criminal or a banned entity like a terrorist.

title: Customer Due Diligence Requirements
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: The nature and extent of due diligence will depend on the risk perceived by the bank. For the purpose of risk categorisation, individuals (other than High Net Worth) and entities whose identities and sources of wealth can be easily identified and transactions in whose accounts by and large conform to the known profile, may be categorised as low risk.
description: Banks must perform customer due diligence based on risk categorization.
plain_english: This means: Banks must assess customer risk and perform due diligence accordingly. Low-risk customers require basic verification, while high-risk customers require enhanced due diligence.
violation_message_template: Customer due diligence not performed according to risk category for {customer_id}

title: Customer Profile Confidentiality
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: The customer profile will be a confidential document and details contained therein shall not be divulged for cross selling or any other purposes.
description: Banks must keep customer profiles confidential.
plain_english: This means: Banks must not share customer profile information for any purpose other than risk assessment.
violation_message_template: Customer profile confidentiality breached for {customer_id}

title: Customer Identification Procedure
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: The policy approved by the Board of banks should clearly spell out the Customer Identification Procedure to be carried out at different stages i.e. while establishing a banking relationship; carrying out a financial transaction or when the bank has a doubt about the authenticity/veracity or the adequacy of the previously obtained customer identification data.
description: Banks must have a clear customer identification procedure in place, approved by their Board, to verify customer identities at various stages.
plain_english: This means: Banks must have a clear plan to verify who their customers are, and they must follow this plan when customers open accounts, make transactions, or when they suspect the customer's information may not be accurate.

title: Customer Identification Requirements
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Banks need to obtain sufficient information necessary to establish, to their satisfaction, the identity of each new customer, whether regular or occasional, and the purpose of the intended nature of banking relationship.
description: Banks must obtain enough information to verify the identity of each new customer and understand the purpose of their banking relationship.
plain_english: This means: Banks must gather enough information to know who their customers are and why they are banking with them.

title: Ongoing Monitoring of Transactions
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Ongoing monitoring is an essential element of effective KYC procedures. Banks can effectively control and reduce their risk only if they have an understanding of the normal and reasonable activity of the customer so that they have the means of identifying transactions that fall outside the regular pattern of activity.
description: Banks must monitor transactions to identify unusual activity.
plain_english: This means: Banks must regularly review customer transactions to detect any unusual patterns. They should understand what normal activity looks like for each customer.

title: Monitoring Threshold Limits
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: The bank may prescribe threshold limits for a particular category of accounts and pay particular attention to the transactions which exceed these limits.
description: Banks should set threshold limits for account transactions.
plain_english: This means: Banks should set limits for transactions based on account type and closely watch transactions that exceed those limits.

title: Identifying Unusual Transactions
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Banks should pay special attention to all complex, unusually large transactions and all unusual patterns which have no apparent economic or visible lawful purpose.
description: Banks must identify complex or unusually large transactions.
plain_english: This means: Banks should pay close attention to transactions that are complex, unusually large, or seem to have no clear purpose.

title: Record Keeping for Transactions
act_section: Section 12 of PML Act, 2002
source_clause: Banks should ensure that a record of transactions in the accounts is preserved and maintained as required in terms of section 12 of the PML Act, 2002.
description: Banks must maintain records of transactions as per the PML Act, 2002.
plain_english: This means: Banks must keep records of all transactions in customer accounts as required by the PML Act, 2002. These records must be preserved and maintained properly.
violation_message_template: Failure to maintain records of transactions as required by the PML Act, 2002 for {account_id} of {customer_name}

title: Reporting Suspicious Transactions
act_section: Section 12 of PML Act, 2002
source_clause: It may also be ensured that transactions of suspicious nature and/ or any other type of transaction notified under section 12 of the PML Act, 2002, is reported to the appropriate law enforcement authority.
description: Banks must report suspicious transactions to the law enforcement authority.
plain_english: This means: Banks must report transactions that seem suspicious or are notified under the PML Act, 2002 to the appropriate law enforcement authority.
violation_message_template: Failure to report suspicious transaction for {transaction_id} of {customer_name} to law enforcement authority

title: Cash Transaction Reporting
source_clause: Banks should ensure that its branches continue to maintain proper record of all cash transactions (deposits and withdrawals) of Rs.10 lakh and above.
description: Banks must maintain records of cash transactions above Rs.10 lakh.
plain_english: This means: Banks must keep records of all cash transactions (deposits and withdrawals) that are Rs.10 lakh or more.
violation_message_template: Failure to maintain record of cash transaction of {amount} for {customer_name}

title: KYC Programme Implementation
source_clause: The Board of Directors of the bank should ensure that an effective KYC programme is put in place by establishing appropriate procedures and ensuring their effective implementation.
description: Banks must implement an effective KYC programme.
plain_english: This means: The bank's Board of Directors must ensure that a proper KYC programme is in place and being followed.
violation_message_template: Failure to implement effective KYC programme for {customer_name}

title: Employee Training Programme
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Banks must have an ongoing employee training programme so that the members of the staff are adequately trained in KYC procedures.
description: Banks are required to have a continuous employee training program to ensure staff are adequately trained in KYC procedures.
plain_english: This means: Banks must train their employees regularly on KYC procedures. The training should cover KYC policies and their implementation.

title: Customer Education
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: There is, therefore, a need for banks to prepare specific literature/ pamphlets etc. so as to educate the customer of the objectives of the KYC programme.
description: Banks are required to prepare educational materials to inform customers about the objectives of the KYC program.
plain_english: This means: Banks must create and provide information to customers about why KYC procedures are necessary.

title: KYC for Electronic Cards
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Banks should ensure that appropriate KYC procedures are duly applied before issuing the cards to the customers.
description: Banks must apply KYC procedures before issuing electronic cards to customers.
plain_english: This means: Banks must perform KYC checks before giving customers electronic cards.

title: Audit Committee Compliance
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: The compliance in this regard may be put up before the Audit Committee of the Board on quarterly intervals.
description: Banks are required to report KYC compliance to the Audit Committee of the Board on a quarterly basis.
plain_english: This means: Banks must report their KYC compliance to the Audit Committee every quarter.

title: KYC for Existing Accounts
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Banks were advised vide our circulars DBOD.AML.BC.47/14.01.001/2003-04, DBOD.AML.129/14.01.001/2003-04 and DBOD.AML.BC.No.101/14.01.001/ 2003-04 dated November 24, 2003, December 16, 2003 and June 21, 2004 respectively to apply the KYC norms advised vide our circular DBOD. No. AML.BC.18/ 14.01.001/ 2002-03 dated August 16, 2002 to all the existing customers in a time bound manner.
description: Banks must apply KYC norms to existing customers based on materiality and risk.
plain_english: This means: Banks must apply Know Your Customer (KYC) rules to existing customers based on how risky they are. Banks should monitor transactions in these accounts and review customer information if anything unusual happens.

title: Monitoring Existing Accounts
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: transactions in existing accounts should be continuously monitored and any unusual pattern in the operation of the account should trigger a review of the CDD measures.
description: Banks must continuously monitor transactions in existing accounts.
plain_english: This means: Banks must keep an eye on transactions in existing accounts and review customer information if anything unusual happens.

title: KYC for High-Risk Accounts
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: all the existing accounts of companies, firms, trusts, charities, religious organizations and other institutions are subjected to minimum KYC standards which would establish the identity of the natural/legal person and those of the 'beneficial owners'.
description: Banks must apply minimum KYC standards to high-risk accounts.
plain_english: This means: Banks must verify the identity of customers and beneficial owners for high-risk accounts.

title: Closure of Non-Cooperative Accounts
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Where the bank is unable to apply appropriate KYC measures due to non-furnishing of information and /or non-cooperation by the customer, the bank may consider closing the account or terminating the banking/business relationship after issuing due notice to the customer explaining the reasons for taking such a decision.
description: Banks may close accounts of non-cooperative customers.
plain_english: This means: If a customer doesn't provide required information or cooperate, the bank may close their account after giving a notice.

title: Applicability to Overseas Branches
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: The above guidelines shall also apply to the branches and majority owned subsidiaries located abroad, especially, in countries which do not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations, to the extent local laws permit.
description: Banks must apply guidelines to overseas branches and subsidiaries.
plain_english: This means: Banks must follow these guidelines in their overseas branches and subsidiaries, if local laws allow.

title: Appointment of Principal Officer
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Banks may appoint a senior management officer to be designated as Principal Officer. Principal Officer shall be located at the head/corporate office of the bank and shall be responsible for monitoring and reporting of all transactions and sharing of information as required under the law.
description: Banks must appoint a Principal Officer.
plain_english: This means: Banks should appoint a senior officer as Principal Officer to handle reporting and information sharing.

title: Customer Identification for Trust/Nominee Accounts
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Banks should determine whether the customer is acting on behalf of another person as trustee/nominee or any other intermediary. If so, banks may insist on receipt of satisfactory evidence of the identity of the intermediaries and of the persons on whose behalf they are acting, as also obtain details of the nature of the trust or other arrangements in place.
description: Banks must verify identities for trust/nominee accounts.
plain_english: This means: Banks must verify the identity of people behind trust or nominee accounts.

title: Verification of Beneficial Owners
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Banks need to be vigilant against business entities being used by individuals as a ‘front’ for maintaining accounts with banks. Banks should examine the control structure of the entity, determine the source of funds and identify the natural persons who have a controlling interest and who comprise the management.
description: Banks must verify the control structure and beneficial owners of business entities
plain_english: This means: Banks must check who really controls a business entity and who benefits from its accounts. They must identify the natural persons with controlling interest and management roles.
violation_message_template: The bank failed to verify the beneficial owners of {account_id} held by {customer_name}

title: Identification of Beneficial Owners in Pooled Accounts
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Where funds held by the intermediaries are not co-mingled at the bank and there are 'sub-accounts', each of them attributable to a beneficial owner, all the beneficial owners must be identified.
description: Banks must identify beneficial owners in pooled accounts
plain_english: This means: If a professional intermediary manages multiple accounts, the bank must identify the beneficial owner of each account.
violation_message_template: The bank failed to identify the beneficial owners of pooled accounts managed by {customer_name}

title: Due Diligence on Intermediaries
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Where the banks rely on the 'customer due diligence' (CDD) done by an intermediary, they should satisfy themselves that the intermediary is regulated and supervised and has adequate systems in place to comply with the KYC requirements.
description: Banks must ensure intermediaries comply with KYC
plain_english: This means: If a bank relies on an intermediary's customer due diligence, it must ensure the intermediary is regulated and can comply with KYC requirements.
violation_message_template: The bank failed to ensure {intermediary_name} complies with KYC requirements

title: PEP Customer Due Diligence
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Banks should gather sufficient information on any person/customer of this category intending to establish a relationship and check all the information available on the person in the public domain. Banks should verify the identify of the person and seek information about the sources of funds before accepting the PEP as a customer.
description: Banks must conduct enhanced due diligence on Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) before opening an account.
plain_english: This means: When a bank is approached by a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) to open an account, the bank must gather enough information about the PEP, verify their identity, and understand the source of their funds.
violation_message_template: The bank failed to conduct proper due diligence on a PEP customer {customer_name} when opening their account {account_id}.

title: Non-Face-to-Face Customer Due Diligence
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: In the case of non-face-to-face customers, apart from applying the usual customer identification procedures, there must be specific and adequate procedures to mitigate the higher risk involved.
description: Banks must have specific procedures to mitigate risks for non-face-to-face customers.
plain_english: This means: When a customer opens an account without visiting the bank branch, the bank must have extra procedures in place to manage the higher risk.
violation_message_template: The bank failed to implement proper procedures for non-face-to-face customer {customer_name} account opening {account_id}.

title: Correspondent Banking Due Diligence
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Banks should gather sufficient information to understand fully the nature of the business of the correspondent/respondent bank.
description: Banks must conduct due diligence on correspondent banks.
plain_english: This means: Banks must gather enough information to understand the business of the other bank when establishing a correspondent banking relationship.

title: Correspondent Banking Relationship Approval
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: While it is desirable that such relationships should be established only with the approval of the Board, in case the Boards of some banks wish to delegate the power to an administrative authority, they may delegate the power to a committee headed by the Chairman/CEO of the bank while laying down clear parameters for approving such relationships.
description: Correspondent banking relationships require Board approval or delegated authority.
plain_english: This means: Banks should get approval from the Board or a designated committee before establishing a correspondent banking relationship.

title: Payable-Through-Accounts Due Diligence
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: In the case of payable-through-accounts, the correspondent bank should be satisfied that the respondent bank has verified the identity of the customers having direct access to the accounts and is undertaking ongoing 'due diligence' on them.
description: Correspondent banks must ensure respondent banks verify customer identities for payable-through-accounts.
plain_english: This means: The correspondent bank must ensure the respondent bank checks the identity of customers with direct access to payable-through-accounts and continues to monitor them.

title: Shell Bank Relationships
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Banks should refuse to enter into a correspondent relationship with a 'shell bank' (i.e. a bank which is incorporated in a country where it has no physical presence and is unaffiliated to any regulated financial group).
description: Banks are prohibited from establishing relationships with shell banks.
plain_english: This means: Banks cannot establish correspondent banking relationships with shell banks.

title: Respondent Bank Due Diligence
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Banks should ensure that their respondent banks have anti money laundering policies and procedures in place and apply enhanced 'due diligence' procedures for transactions carried out through the correspondent accounts.
description: Banks must ensure respondent banks have AML policies and apply enhanced due diligence for correspondent account transactions.
plain_english: This means: Banks must check that their correspondent banks have rules to prevent money laundering and carefully monitor transactions.
violation_message_template: Failure to ensure respondent bank has AML policies and procedures in place for correspondent account transactions.

title: Respondent Bank Relationship Caution
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Banks should also guard against establishing relationships with respondent foreign financial institutions that permit their accounts to be used by shell banks.
description: Banks are prohibited from establishing relationships with respondent banks that allow shell banks to use their accounts.
plain_english: This means: Banks must not work with foreign banks that let shell banks use their accounts.
violation_message_template: Establishing relationship with respondent bank that allows shell bank to use its accounts.

title: KYC Compliance Deadline
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs were advised to ensure that they are fully compliant with the instructions before December 31, 2005.
description: NBFCs must comply with KYC guidelines by a specified deadline.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs had to follow KYC guidelines by December 31, 2005. If not, they risk regulatory action.
violation_message_template: KYC compliance deadline missed for {account_id} on {flag_date}

title: Confidentiality of Customer Information
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: information collected from the customer for the purpose of opening of account should be kept as confidential and not divulge any details thereof for cross selling or any other purposes.
description: NBFCs must keep customer information confidential.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must not share customer information for cross-selling or other purposes without consent.
violation_message_template: Customer information breach for {customer_id} on {flag_date}

title: KYC Guidelines for Authorized Persons
act_section: Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (Chapter IV)
source_clause: Adherence to Know Your Customer (KYC) guidelines by NBFC and persons authorised by NBFCs including brokers/agents etc.
description: NBFCs and authorized persons must follow KYC guidelines.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs and their authorized persons, like brokers or agents, must follow KYC guidelines to prevent money laundering.
violation_message_template: KYC non-compliance by {authorized_person} for {customer_id} on {flag_date}

title: KYC Compliance Responsibility
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: The NBFC should make available all information to the Bank to verify the compliance with the KYC guidelines and accept full consequences of any violation by the persons authorised by NBFCs including brokers/agents etc. who are operating on its behalf.
description: NBFCs are responsible for ensuring KYC compliance by authorized persons.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must provide all information to the Bank to verify KYC compliance by authorized persons. They must also accept consequences of any violations.

title: KYC for Existing RNBC Customers
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: For the existing customers, initially, KYC guidelines should be complied in respect of large customers whose aggregate deposit exceeds Rs.1 lakh.
description: RNBCs must comply with KYC guidelines for existing large customers.
plain_english: This means: RNBCs must follow KYC guidelines for existing customers with deposits over Rs.1 lakh.

title: Due Diligence for Authorized Persons
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs should put in place a process of due diligence in respect of persons authorised by NBFCs including brokers/agents etc. collecting deposits on behalf of the company through a uniform policy for appointment and detailed verification.
description: NBFCs must conduct due diligence on authorized persons.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must have a process to verify the background of authorized persons collecting deposits.

title: KYC Procedure Simplification
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: It was clarified in March 2006 that although flexibility in the requirement of documents of identity and proof of address has been provided in the circular mentioned above yet there may be instances where certain persons, especially, those belonging to low income group both in urban and rural areas may not be able to produce such documents to satisfy the NBFC about their identity and address. Hence, it has been decided to further simplify the KYC procedure for opening accounts by NBFCs for those persons who intend to keep balances not exceeding rupees fifty thousand (Rs. 50,000/-) in all their accounts taken together  and the total credit  in all the accounts taken together  is not expected to exceed rupees one lakh
description: NBFCs are required to simplify KYC procedures for customers with balances not exceeding Rs. 50,000 and total credit not exceeding Rs. 1 lakh.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must simplify Know Your Customer procedures for customers who plan to keep balances below Rs. 50,000 and total credits below Rs. 1 lakh across all their accounts. This helps low-income individuals who may not have necessary documents.

title: Deposit Receipt Requirements
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: All deposit receipts should bear the name and Registered Office address of the NBFC and must invariably indicate the name of the persons authorised  by NBFCs including brokers/agents etc. and their addresses who mobilised the deposit and the link office with the telephone number of such officer and/or persons authorised  by NBFCs including brokers/agents etc in order that there is a clear indication of the identifiable contact with the field persons
description: NBFCs must include specific details on deposit receipts.
plain_english: This means: All deposit receipts must have the NBFC's name and address, and clearly mention the authorized person's name, address, and contact details.

title: KYC Customer Identification Documents
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs are advised to take a review of their extant internal instructions in this regard. It is clarified that permanent correct address, as referred to in Annex-VIII of this circular, means the address at which a person usually resides and can be taken as the address as mentioned in a utility bill or any other document accepted by the NBFC for verification of the address of the customer.
description: NBFCs must review internal instructions for customer identification and verify customer addresses through utility bills or other documents.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs should check their current rules for identifying customers and make sure they are following the guidelines. They should verify a customer's address with documents like utility bills.

title: Periodic Review of Risk Categorization
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs are required to put in place a system of periodical review of risk categorisation of accounts and the need for applying enhanced due diligence measures in case of higher risk perception on a customer.
description: NBFCs are required to periodically review risk categorization of accounts and apply enhanced due diligence measures for higher risk customers.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must regularly review the risk level of their customers' accounts and take extra precautions for customers with higher risk.

title: KYC/AML Guidelines for Overseas Branches
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: KYC/AML guidelines issued by Reserve Bank of India shall also apply to their branches and majority owned subsidiaries located outside India, especially, in countries which do not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations, to the extent local laws permit.
description: NBFCs must apply KYC/AML guidelines to overseas branches and subsidiaries.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must follow RBI's KYC/AML guidelines for their overseas branches and subsidiaries, where permitted by local laws.
violation_message_template: KYC/AML guidelines not applied to overseas branch {branch_name}

title: Suspicious Transaction Reporting
act_section: PMLA Rules
source_clause: NBFCs are, therefore, advised to develop suitable mechanism through appropriate policy framework for enhanced monitoring of accounts suspected of having terrorist links and swift identification of the transactions and making suitable reports to the Financial Intelligence Unit – India (FIU-IND) on priority.
description: NBFCs must report suspicious transactions to FIU-IND.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must monitor accounts for terrorist links, identify suspicious transactions, and report them to FIU-IND promptly.
violation_message_template: Suspicious transaction not reported to FIU-IND for {customer_id}

title: Screening for UN Sanctions List
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs are advised that before opening any new account it should be ensured that the name/s of the proposed customer does not appear in the list. Further, NBFCs should scan all existing accounts to ensure that no account is held by or linked to any of the entities or individuals included in the list.
description: NBFCs must check customers against the UN sanctions list.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must check if a customer's name is on the UN sanctions list before opening a new account and review existing accounts to ensure no one on the list has an account.
violation_message_template: The customer {customer_name} has an account despite being on the UN sanctions list.

title: KYC/AML Screening in Recruitment
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: It would, therefore, be necessary that adequate screening mechanism is put in place by NBFCs as an integral part of their recruitment/hiring process of personnel.
description: NBFCs must implement screening in their hiring process.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must have a screening process for hiring personnel to prevent criminals from working there.
violation_message_template: The employee {employee_name} was hired without proper screening.

title: Suspicious Transaction Alerts
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs may consider the indicative list of suspicious activities contained in Annex-V of the CC No.126 dated August 05, 2008.
description: NBFCs should use guidelines for suspicious transactions.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs should use the list of suspicious activities to generate alerts for transactions that might be unusual or suspicious.
violation_message_template: The transaction {transaction_id} was not flagged as suspicious despite matching the indicative list.

title: Compliance with Guidelines
act_section: Sections 45K and 45L of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
source_clause: These guidelines are issued under Sections 45K and 45L of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 and any contravention of or non-compliance with the same may attract penalties under the relevant provisions of the Act.
description: NBFCs must comply with these guidelines.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must follow these guidelines and any failure to do so can result in penalties.
violation_message_template: The NBFC failed to comply with the guidelines resulting in a penalty.

title: PEP Account Monitoring
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: in the event of an existing customer or the beneficial owner of an existing account, subsequently becoming a PEP, NBFCs (including RNBCs) should obtain senior management approval to continue the business relationship and subject the account to the CDD measures as applicable to the customers of PEP category including enhanced monitoring on an ongoing basis.
description: NBFCs must monitor PEP accounts and obtain senior management approval to continue business relationships with PEP customers.
plain_english: This means: If a customer becomes a politically exposed person (PEP), the NBFC must get senior management approval to keep the account open and closely monitor it.
violation_message_template: NBFC failed to obtain senior management approval for PEP account {account_id} of customer {customer_name}

title: Principal Officer Independence
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs (including RNBCs) should ensure that the Principal Officer is able to act independently and report directly to the senior management or to the Board of Directors.
description: NBFCs must ensure Principal Officer independence and direct reporting to senior management or the Board of Directors.
plain_english: This means: The Principal Officer must be able to work independently and report directly to senior management or the Board of Directors.
violation_message_template: NBFC failed to ensure Principal Officer independence for {Principal Officer}

title: High-Risk Country Monitoring
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: All NBFCs and RNBCs are accordingly advised to take into account risks arising from the deficiencies in AML/CFT regime of Iran, Uzbekistan, Pakistan, Turkmenistan and Sao Tome and Principe.
description: NBFCs must monitor transactions related to high-risk countries.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must consider the risks of doing business with customers from Iran, Uzbekistan, Pakistan, Turkmenistan, and Sao Tome and Principe.
violation_message_template: NBFC failed to monitor high-risk country transactions from {country}
condition_value: Iran, Uzbekistan, Pakistan, Turkmenistan, Sao Tome and Principe

title: Restrictions on Professional Intermediaries
act_section: Section 45K and 45L of Reserve Bank of India Regulation Act, 1934
source_clause: NBFCs should not allow opening and/or holding of an account on behalf of a client/s by professional intermediaries, like Lawyers and Chartered Accountants, etc., who are unable to disclose true identity of the owner of the account/funds due to any professional obligation of customer confidentiality.
description: NBFCs are prohibited from allowing professional intermediaries to open or hold accounts if they cannot disclose the true identity of the account owner due to confidentiality obligations.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs cannot allow professionals like lawyers or accountants to open or manage accounts if they can't reveal who really owns the account. This is to prevent money laundering.
violation_message_template: The NBFC allowed a professional intermediary to open/hold an account for a client without disclosing the true identity of the account owner.

title: Consideration of FATF Recommendations
act_section: Master Circular No. 184 dated July 01, 2010
source_clause: NBFCs were advised to take into account risks arising from the deficiencies in AML/CFT regime of the jurisdictions included in the FATF Statement.
description: NBFCs are required to consider risks from jurisdictions with AML/CFT deficiencies as per FATF Statements.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must consider the money laundering risks when dealing with countries that have weak anti-money laundering rules.
violation_message_template: The NBFC failed to consider AML/CFT risks when dealing with a jurisdiction with known deficiencies.

title: Countermeasures for High-Risk Jurisdictions
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: All NBFCs/RNBCs were accordingly advised to take into account risks arising from the deficiencies in AML/CFT regime of these countries.
description: NBFCs/RNBCs must consider risks from jurisdictions with strategic AML/CFT deficiencies.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs and RNBCs should be cautious when dealing with countries that have weaknesses in their anti-money laundering and combating the financing of terrorism systems.

title: Acknowledgement of Circular Receipt
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: Further all NBFCs/RNBCs were advised to acknowledge receipt of this circular to be submitted by the Compliance officer/ Principal Officer of the NBFCs to the concerned Regional Office of DNBS in whose jurisdiction the NBFC/RNBC is functioning.
description: NBFCs/RNBCs must acknowledge receipt of circular.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs and RNBCs must confirm that they have received this circular by sending a notification to their regional office.

title: Appointment of Principal Officer
act_section: Section 12 of PMLA 2002
source_clause: NBFCs were advised to appoint a Principal Officer and put in place a system of internal reporting of suspicious transactions and cash transactions of Rs.10 lakh and above.
description: NBFCs must appoint a Principal Officer to oversee AML/CFT compliance.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must have a Principal Officer in charge of reporting suspicious transactions and large cash transactions.

title: Internal Reporting of Suspicious Transactions
act_section: Section 12 of PMLA 2002
source_clause: NBFCs were advised to appoint a Principal Officer and put in place a system of internal reporting of suspicious transactions and cash transactions of Rs.10 lakh and above.
description: NBFCs must have a system for internal reporting of suspicious transactions.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must have a system in place to report suspicious transactions internally.

title: Reporting Cash Transactions above Rs.10 lakh
act_section: Section 12 of PMLA 2002
source_clause: NBFCs were advised to appoint a Principal Officer and put in place a system of internal reporting of suspicious transactions and cash transactions of Rs.10 lakh and above.
description: NBFCs must report cash transactions exceeding Rs.10 lakh.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must report cash transactions of Rs.10 lakh or more internally.

title: Cash Transaction Reporting Threshold
act_section: Rule 3 of PMLA Rules 2005
source_clause: NBFCs should introduce a system of maintaining proper record of transactions prescribed under Rule 3, as mentioned below: all cash transactions of the value of more than rupees ten lakh or its equivalent in foreign currency;
description: NBFCs must record cash transactions over Rs. 10 lakh.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must keep a record of all cash transactions that are more than Rs. 10 lakh or its equivalent in foreign currency.
violation_message_template: The NBFC failed to report a cash transaction of {amount} exceeding the threshold of Rs. 10 lakh.

title: Aggregated Cash Transaction Reporting Threshold
act_section: Rule 3 of PMLA Rules 2005
source_clause: all series of cash transactions integrally connected to each other which have been valued below rupees ten lakh or its equivalent in foreign currency where such series of transactions have taken place within a month and the aggregate value of such transactions exceeds rupees ten lakh;
description: NBFCs must record aggregated cash transactions over Rs. 10 lakh within a month.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must keep a record of a series of cash transactions that are below Rs. 10 lakh each but collectively exceed Rs. 10 lakh within a month.
violation_message_template: The NBFC failed to report aggregated cash transactions of {amount} exceeding the threshold of Rs. 10 lakh within a month.

title: Suspicious Transaction Reporting
act_section: Rule 3 of PMLA Rules 2005
source_clause: all suspicious transactions whether or not made in cash and in manner as mentioned in the Rules framed by Government of India under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002.
description: NBFCs must report suspicious transactions.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must report all suspicious transactions, whether in cash or not, as per the Rules framed by the Government of India under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002.
violation_message_template: The NBFC failed to report a suspicious transaction.

title: Record Keeping Requirements
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs should take appropriate steps to evolve a system for proper maintenance and preservation of account information in a manner that allows data to be retrieved easily and quickly whenever required or when requested by the competent authorities.
description: NBFCs must maintain and preserve account information.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must have a system to properly maintain and preserve account information so that it can be easily retrieved when needed or requested by competent authorities.
violation_message_template: The NBFC failed to maintain and preserve account information.

title: Record Retention Period
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs should maintain for at least ten years from the date of cessation of transaction between the NBFCs and the client, all necessary records of transactions, both domestic or international, which will permit reconstruction of individual transactions (including the amounts and types of currency involved if any) so as to provide, if necessary, evidence for prosecution of persons involved in criminal activity.
description: NBFCs must retain records for at least 10 years.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must keep all necessary records of transactions for at least 10 years from the date the transaction with the client ends.
violation_message_template: The NBFC failed to retain records for {record_age_years} years.

title: Record Retention Period
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs should ensure that records pertaining to the identification of the customer and his address (e.g. copies of documents like passports, identity cards, driving licenses, PAN, utility bills etc.) obtained while opening the account and during the course of business relationship, are properly preserved for at least ten years after the business relationship is ended.
description: NBFCs must retain customer identification records for at least ten years after the business relationship ends.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must keep customer identification records for at least 10 years after the business relationship ends. These records include copies of passports, identity cards, and utility bills.
violation_message_template: The NBFC {name} failed to retain customer identification records for {customer_name} for at least 10 years after the business relationship ended on {date}.

title: Reporting to FIU-India
act_section: Master Circular DNBS(PD) CC No.231/03.10.42/2011-12 dated July 1, 2011
source_clause: NBFCs are required to report information relating to cash and suspicious transactions to the Director, Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND).
description: NBFCs must report cash and suspicious transactions to FIU-IND.
plain_english: This means: NBFCs must report cash and suspicious transactions to the Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND).
violation_message_template: The NBFC {name} failed to report {transaction_type} transaction to FIU-IND on {date}.
